فَمَن مُبلغٌ عَني قُرَيشًا رسَالة ... فَهَلْ بَعدَهُم فِي المجْد مِنْ مُتَكرّم ...
Who will convey from me a message to Quraysh? Is there, after them, anyone in glory who is more noble?

بِأَنَّ أخاكمُ فاعلَمنّ مُحَمَّدًا ... تَليدُ النَّدى بينَ الحَجُون وزَمْزَم ...
That your brother, Muhammad, know well, is the inherited generosity between al-Hajun and Zamzam...

فَدينُوا لَهُ بِالْحَقِّ تَجْسُمْ أمُورُكم ... وتَسْمُوا منَ الدنْيا إِلَى كُل مُعْظَم ...
So submit to him in truth, and your affairs will be set right, and you will rise from this world to every exalted height...

نَبِيٌّ تلافَته منَ اللَّهِ رَحَمةٌ ... وَلَا تَسْألُوهُ أمْرَ غَيب مُرَجَّم ...
He is a Prophet whom mercy from God has embraced; and do not ask him about a hidden matter that is conjectured...

فَقَدْ كانَ فِي بَدْر لَعَمْري عِبرَةٌ ... لَكُم يَا قُرَيش والقَليب المُلَمَّم ...
Indeed, by my life, there was a lesson for you at Badr, O Quraysh, and at the well filled with corpses...

غَدَاة أتَى فِي الخَزْرَجيَّةِ عامِدًا ... إليكُم مُطيعًا للعَظيمِ المُكَرّم ...
On the morning he came, purposefully, in the Khazrajite (battle array), to you, obedient to the Mighty, the Generous...

مُعَانًا برُوح القُدْس يَنْكي عَدوه ... رَسُولا مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ حَقّا بِمَعْلم ...
Aided by the Holy Spirit, who inflicts defeat upon his enemy, a messenger from the Most Merciful, truly and clearly marked...

رَسُولا مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ يَتْلُو كِتابَهُ ... فَلَمّا أنارَ الحَقّ لَمْ يَتَلعْثَم ...
A messenger from the Most Merciful, reciting His Book; and when the truth shone forth, he did not falter...

أرَى أمْرَهُ يَزْدَادُ فِي كُلّ مَوْطن ... عُلُوّا لأمرْ حَمَّه اللهُ مُحْكَم [[انظر: السيرة النبوية لابن هشام (٢/١٩٥) .]]
I see his affair increasing in every situation, in exaltation, by a matter God has decreed and made firm. [See: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (2/195).]

وَقَدْ أَوْرَدَ ابْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ، هاهنا أَشْعَارًا كَثِيرَةً، فِيهَا آدَابٌ وَمَوَاعِظُ وَحِكَمٌ، وَتَفَاصِيلُ لِلْقِصَّةِ، تَرَكْنَا بَاقِيهَا اخْتِصَارًا وَاكْتِفَاءً بِمَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ، وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ وَالْمِنَّةُ.
Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, cited here many verses, containing courtesies, admonitions and wisdom, and details of the story. We have left out the remainder for brevity and being content with what we have mentioned. To God belongs all praise and grace.

قَالَ ابْنُ إِسْحَاقَ: كَانَتْ وَقْعَةُ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ بَعْدَ وَقْعَةِ أُحُدٍ وَبَعْدَ بِئْرِ مَعُونَةَ. وَحَكَى الْبُخَارِيُّ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: كَانَتْ وَقْعَةُ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ بَعْدَ بَدْرٍ بِسِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ [[صحيح البخاري (٧/٣٢٩) "فتح".]] .
Ibn Ishaq said: The incident of Banu al-Nadir occurred after the Battle of Uhud and after the well of Ma'una. Al-Bukhari related, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, that he said: The incident of Banu al-Nadir occurred six months after Badr. [Sahih al-Bukhari (7/329), Fath.]

**Commentary on Surah al-Hashr**

[It was also said by Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat Bani an-Nadir"] [[Addition from A.]]. It is a Medinan surah.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?" He said: "It was revealed concerning Bani an-Nadir." Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it by another route, from Hushaym, with the same chain [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4882, and Sahih Muslim, no. 3031.]]. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?" He said: "Say: Surat an-Nadir" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4883.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

He, exalted is He, informs that everything in the heavens and everything on the earth glorifies Him, extols Him, sanctifies Him, prays to Him, and affirms His oneness [[In M: "wahdahu" (alone).]], as in His saying: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. There is not a thing but that it glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44]. His saying ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ means: the Unassailable in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His decree and His legislation.

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book﴾ refers to the Jews of Bani an-Nadir. This was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, az-Zuhri, and others. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, he made a truce with them and gave them a covenant and a guarantee that he would not fight them and they would not fight him. Then they broke the covenant that was between them and him, so Allah brought upon them His might, which cannot be repelled, and sent down upon them His decree, which cannot be averted. The Prophet ﷺ then exiled them and expelled them from their fortified strongholds, which the Muslims had not expected to conquer, and they themselves thought that these would protect them from the might of Allah. But they availed them nothing against Allah, and there came upon them what they had not imagined. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them away and expelled them from Medina. A group of them went to Adhruʿat in the uplands of Syria, which is the land of the gathering and the assembling, and another group went to Khaybar. He had settled them there on the condition that they could take whatever their camels could carry. They would ruin what was in their houses of movable items that could be carried with them. Therefore He said: ﴿They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of insight﴾, that is: reflect upon the outcome of those who opposed the command of Allah, opposed His Messenger, and denied His Book, and how the painful punishment that He reserves for them in the Hereafter, together with the humiliating might that befalls them in this world, will come upon them.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Dawud and Sufyan narrated to us; 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, that the disbelieving Quraysh wrote to Ibn Ubayy and those with him who worshipped idols from the Aws and the Khazraj, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Medina before the Battle of Badr: "You have sheltered our companion, and we swear by Allah that we will certainly fight him, or you will expel him, or we will all march against you until we kill your fighting men and take your women captive." When this reached 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those with him among the idol-worshippers, they gathered to fight the Prophet ﷺ. When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he came to them and said: "The threat of Quraysh has reached you in its extremity. Their scheming against you is no more than what they wish to scheme against themselves. Do you wish to fight your own sons and brothers?" When they heard this from the Prophet ﷺ, they dispersed. This reached the disbelieving Quraysh, and after the Battle of Badr the disbelieving Quraysh wrote to the Jews: "You are the people of the ring-shaped fortifications and the strongholds, and you must fight alongside our companion, or we will do such-and-such. Nothing will stand between us and the ornaments of your women," meaning the anklets. When their letter reached the Prophet ﷺ, Bani an-Nadir gathered to act treacherously. They sent to the Prophet ﷺ: "Come out to us with thirty men of your companions, and thirty of our rabbis will come out, so that we may meet at a neutral place and they will hear from you. If they believe you and have faith in you, we will have faith in you too." When the next day came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them with the battalions and besieged them. He said to them: "By Allah, you will not be secure with me except under a covenant that you pledge to me." They refused to give him a covenant, so he fought them that day. Then the following day he went with the battalions against Bani Qurayzah and left Bani an-Nadir, and he called them to make a covenant with him, and they made a covenant, so he turned away from them. Then he went with the battalions against Bani an-Nadir and fought them until they agreed to leave. So Bani an-Nadir departed, taking with them what their camels could carry of their goods, the doors of their houses, and their timber. The date palms of Bani an-Nadir belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone, which Allah had given him and specially assigned to him. So He said: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not press forward against it with horse or camel﴾, meaning: without fighting. The Prophet ﷺ gave most of it to the Emigrants, dividing it among them, and he gave a share to two men of the Ansar who were in need, and no one else of the Ansar was given a share. What remained of it was the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which was in the hands of the family of Fatimah [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3004.]].

We shall mention a summary of the Battle of Bani an-Nadir in brief. And in Allah is the help sought.

The cause of it, as mentioned by the scholars of the campaigns and biographies, was that when the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Bi'r Ma'unah were killed, and they were seventy, only 'Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri escaped. On his way back to Medina he killed two men from Bani 'Amir, and they had a covenant and a safe-conduct from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which 'Amr did not know about. When he returned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed, and he said to him: "You have killed two men, and I will certainly pay their blood-money." There was an alliance and a covenant between Bani an-Nadir and Bani 'Amir. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Bani an-Nadir seeking their help in paying the blood-money for those two men. The dwellings of Bani an-Nadir were outside Medina, a few miles away to its east.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in his book, the Sirah: Then the Messenger of Allah went out to Bani an-Nadir, seeking their help in paying the blood-money for the two slain men from Bani 'Amir, whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri had killed, because of the protection that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had granted them, as Yazid ibn Ruman related to me. There was a pact and an alliance between Bani an-Nadir and Bani 'Amir. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them seeking their help in paying the blood-money for those two slain men, they said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, we will help you in what you wish, regarding what you have sought our help for." Then some of them withdrew to speak privately with one another, and they said: "You will never find the man in a situation like this, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is beside a wall of their houses. Who will climb onto this house and drop a stone on him, so that he will rid us of him?" 'Amr ibn Jihash ibn Ka'b, one of them, volunteered for this and said: "I will do it." He climbed up to drop a stone on him as he had said, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with a group of his companions, among them Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them. Then the news came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from heaven of what the people intended, so he stood up and went back toward Medina. When the Prophet ﷺ was delayed, his companions rose to look for him, and they met a man coming from Medina and asked him about him. He said: "I saw him entering Medina." So the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came until they reached him, and he told them what had happened, that the Jews had intended treachery against him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them to prepare for war against them and to march against them. Then he set out until he arrived at them, and they took refuge from him in their fortresses. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the palm trees to be cut down and burned. They called out to him: "O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption and condemn those who committed it. What is the matter with cutting down and burning the palm trees?"

A group from Bani 'Awf ibn al-Khazraj, among them 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi'ah, Malik ibn Abi Qawqal, Suwayd, and Da'is, had sent to Bani an-Nadir: "Hold firm and defend yourselves, for we will not abandon you. If you are fought, we will fight alongside you, and if you are expelled, we will go out with you." They awaited that support from them, but they did not do so. Allah cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to exile them and to spare their lives, on the condition that they could take whatever their camels could carry of their property, except for the ring-shaped armour. He agreed, and they took from their property whatever the camels could carry. A man among them would dismantle his house from the frame of its door, place it on the back of his camel, and set off with it. Some of them went to Khaybar, and some of them went to Syria, and they left their property to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so it belonged to the Messenger of Allah alone, and he would place it wherever he willed. He divided it among the first Emigrants, to the exclusion of the Ansar, except that Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah mentioned their poverty, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave to them.

He said: None of Bani an-Nadir was spared except two men: Yamin ibn 'Umayr ibn Ka'b ibn 'Amr ibn Jihash, and Abu Sa'd ibn Wahb. They both embraced Islam, retaining their property, and so they secured it.

Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Yamin narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Yamin: "Did you not see what I suffered from your cousin, and what they intended against me?" Yamin ibn 'Umayr then offered a reward to a man on condition that he kill 'Amr ibn Jihash, and he killed him, as they allege.

Ibn Ishaq said: The Surah of al-Hashr was revealed in its entirety concerning Bani an-Nadir [[See: as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (2/190–192) and Tafsir al-Tabari (28/21).]].

Thus Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Ibn Ishaq, in similar terms to what has preceded.

So His saying ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book﴾ refers to Bani an-Nadir, ﴿from their homes at the first gathering﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us; Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever doubts that the land of the gathering is here, meaning Syria, let him recite this verse: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Leave." They said: "To where?" He said: "To the land of the gathering."

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ exiled Bani an-Nadir, he said: "This is the first gathering, and I am following in its trail."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, with the same wording [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/20). Ibn Sa'd also narrated it in at-Tabaqat (2/42) from Hawdhah ibn Khalifah, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, and it is mursal.]].

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 59, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 3):

And His saying: ﴿You did not think that they would leave﴾, meaning: during the period of your siege of them, and its brevity, which was six days, despite the strength of their fortresses and their defences. For this reason He said: ﴿And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but Allah came at them from where they did not expect﴾, meaning: there came to them a command from Allah that had never occurred to them, as He said in another verse: ﴿Those before them had already schemed, so Allah came at their structures from the foundations, and the roof fell down on them from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive﴾ [An-Nahl: 26].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾, meaning: fear, panic and dismay. How could they not experience that, when the one who was supported with terror (ﷺ) had besieged them from a distance of a month's journey? May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾. The interpretation of Ibn Ishaq regarding this has already been mentioned: it is the dismantling of what they had admired of their roofs and doors, and carrying them on camels. Likewise said 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fight them, and whenever he gained control over an alley or a house, he would demolish its walls so that the space would be wide enough for fighting. The Jews, whenever they occupied a place or overpowered an alley or a house, would dig through its back walls, then fortify and barricade them. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So take warning, O you with insight﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Had Allah not decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world﴾, meaning: had Allah not decreed for them this exile, which is their expulsion from their homes and their wealth, they would have had another punishment from Allah, namely killing, captivity and the like. This was said by al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, and by al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, because Allah had decreed for them that He would punish them in the worldly abode, in addition to what He had prepared for them in the Hereafter of the punishment of the Fire of Hell.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to me, from al-Layth, from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, saying: Then came the event of the Banu al-Nadir, who were a group of the Jews, six months after the Battle of Badr. Their dwelling was in one part of Medina, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them until they came down to accept exile, and that they would have whatever wealth and goods the camels could carry, except the weapons (al-halqah), which is the arms. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) exiled them towards Syria. He said: The exile was that it had been prescribed for them in certain verses of the Torah, and they were from a tribe that had not been subjected to exile before what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given power over. And Allah sent down concerning them: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾ up to His saying ﴿and that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾.

ʿIkrimah said: The exile (al-jala') is killing. In another narration from him: it is annihilation.

Qatadah said: The exile is the departure of people from one town to another town.

al-Dahhak said: He exiled them to Syria, and gave every three of them a camel and a water-skin. That is the exile.

The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Ahmad ibn Kamil al-Qadi informed us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-'Awfi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my paternal uncle, from my father, from my grandfather, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had besieged them until he reached every extremity with them, so they offered him what he desired from them. He made peace with them on the condition that he would spare their lives, that he would expel them from their land, their homes and their homelands, and that he would send them to Adhri'at in Syria, and he gave every three of them a camel and a water-skin. The exile (al-jala') is their expulsion from their land to another land. [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi (3/359); its chain is a chain consisting entirely of weak narrators.]

It has also been narrated through Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri, from Ibrahim ibn Ja'far ibn Mahmud ibn Muhammad ibn Maslamah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Muhammad ibn Maslamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him to the Banu al-Nadir and ordered him to give them a respite of three nights for the exile. [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/360).]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: a decisive, binding matter from which they cannot escape.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: Allah did that to them and gave power over them to His Messenger and His believing servants only because they opposed Allah and His Messenger, and denied what Allah had sent down to His earlier messengers regarding the good news of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they recognised that just as they recognise their own sons. Then He said: ﴿And whoever opposes Allah, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾. Al-liyah: a type of date, and it is good quality.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: It is what differs from al-'ajwah and al-barni among dates.

Many of the exegetes said: al-liynah is the varieties of dates other than al-'ajwah.

Ibn Jarir said: It is the whole of the palm trees, and he attributed to Mujahid: and it is also al-Buwayrah. That is because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them, he ordered that their palm trees be cut down, as a humiliation to them, and as intimidation and terror for their hearts. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yazid ibn Ruman, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: [Then the Banu al-Nadir] said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): You forbid corruption, so why do you order the cutting of trees? So Allah sent down this noble verse: meaning, whatever you cut down and whatever trees you left, all of it is by the permission of Allah, His will, His power, and His pleasure. In it is a blow against the enemy, disgrace for them, and the humbling of their noses.

Mujahid said: Some of the emigrants forbade others from cutting palm trees, and they said: They are only the spoils of the Muslims. So the Qur'an was revealed confirming those who forbade cutting them, and permitting those who cut them from sin, and the cutting and leaving were by His permission. This has also been narrated in a raised (marfu') form. al-Nasa'i said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, from 'Affan, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾, he said: They were bringing them down from their fortresses, and they ordered the cutting of palm trees, so this troubled their hearts. The Muslims said: We cut some and left some, so let us ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Is there a reward for us in what we cut? And is there a sin upon us for what we left? So Allah sent down: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down﴾. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11574).]

The hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, Hafs narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Jabir, and from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: He (ﷺ) permitted them to cut palm trees, then he tightened the restriction on them, so they asked the Prophet (ﷺ): O Messenger of Allah, is there a sin upon us for what we cut? Or is there a burden upon us for what we left? So Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah﴾. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (4/135), in which is Sufyan ibn Waki', who is weak. Note: the narration of Sulayman ibn Musa from Jabir I have not found in the printed Musnad of Abu Ya'la, so it may have fallen out.]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut down the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir and burned them.

The two authors of the Sahihs also narrated it through Musa ibn 'Uqbah, with similar wording. [Musnad (2/7); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2021); Sahih Muslim no. (1746).] The wording of al-Bukhari, through 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: al-Nadir and Quraydah fought, so he exiled the Banu al-Nadir and kept Quraydah, and was gracious to them, until Quraydah fought, so he killed their men, took their women, children and wealth and divided them among the Muslims, except for some of them who joined the Prophet (ﷺ), and he granted them safety and they embraced Islam. He also exiled all the Jews of Medina: the Banu Qaynuqa', who were the kin of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, the Jews of the Banu Harithah, and all the Jews in Medina.

Also in both of them, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir and cut them down, and that is al-Buwayrah. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down concerning it: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4884); Sahih Muslim no. (1746).]

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, has, through the narration of Juwayriyah ibn Asma' from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir. [In some manuscripts: "the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir and cut al-Buwayrah"; the phrase "cut al-Buwayrah" is not established in al-Bukhari, and it appears to be an error of a copyist.] And about it Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

The burning at al-Buwayrah, spreading far and wide, was made light in the eyes of the nobles of the Banu Lu'ayy...

Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith replied, saying:

May Allah perpetuate that deed of yours, and the blaze that burned in its surroundings...
You will know which of us will have a delight in it, and you will know which of our lands is Nadir...

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it, and Ibn Ishaq did not mention it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Ka'b ibn Malik said, recalling the exile of the Banu al-Nadir and the killing of Ibn al-Ashraf:

Indeed they were disgraced by their treachery, the Hubur... [the verses as recorded in the source]

أَهْلِي فدَاءٌ لِامْرِئٍ غَير هَالك ... أحَلّ [[في أ: "أجلي".]] اليهودَ بالحَسِى [[في م، أ: "بالحس".]] المُزَنَّم ...
May my family be a ransom for a man who is not destroyed, who settled the Jews at al-Hasi al-Muzannam...

يَقيلُونَ فِي جَمْر الغَضاة وبُدّلُوا ... أهَيضبَ عُودًا بالوَدي المُكَمَّم ...
They take their midday rest on the embers of the ghada tree, and they were exchanged for a rain-drenched stick in the valley of al-Wadi al-Mukammam...

فَإِنْ يَكُ ظَني صَادقًا بمُحَمد ... يَرَوا خَيلَه بينَ الصِّلَا وَيَرمْرَم [[في أ: "بين الصفا وبزمزم".]]
So if my assumption about Muhammad is true, they will see his horses between al-Sila and Yarmaram [[In A: "between al-Safa and Zamzam".]]...

يَؤمّ بِهَا عَمرو بنُ بُهثَةَ إنَّهُمْ ... عَدُو ما حَيّ صَديق كمُجْرم ...
Amr ibn Buhtha leads them, for they are an enemy, as long as any tribe is a friend like a criminal...

عَلَيهنّ أبطالُ مَساعيرُ فِي الوَغَى ... يَهُزّونَ أطرافَ الوَشيج المُقَوّم ...
Upon them are heroes who kindle the flames of battle, brandishing the tips of straight, well-made spear shafts...

وكُلّ رَقيق الشَّفرتَين مُهَنَّدٍ ... تُورثْنَ مِنْ أزْمان عَادٍ وَجُرْهُمِ ...
And every thin-edged, Indian-made sword, inherited from the times of ʿAd and Jurhum...

فَمَن مُبلغٌ عَني قُرَيشًا رسَالة ... فَهَلْ بَعدَهُم فِي المجْد مِنْ مُتَكرّم ...
Who will convey from me a message to Quraysh? Is there, after them, anyone in glory who is more noble?

بِأَنَّ أخاكمُ فاعلَمنّ مُحَمَّدًا ... تَليدُ النَّدى بينَ الحَجُون وزَمْزَم ...
That your brother, Muhammad, know well, is the inherited generosity between al-Hajun and Zamzam...

فَدينُوا لَهُ بِالْحَقِّ تَجْسُمْ أمُورُكم ... وتَسْمُوا منَ الدنْيا إِلَى كُل مُعْظَم ...
So submit to him in truth, and your affairs will be set right, and you will rise from this world to every exalted height...

نَبِيٌّ تلافَته منَ اللَّهِ رَحَمةٌ ... وَلَا تَسْألُوهُ أمْرَ غَيب مُرَجَّم ...
He is a Prophet whom mercy from God has embraced; and do not ask him about a hidden matter that is conjectured...

فَقَدْ كانَ فِي بَدْر لَعَمْري عِبرَةٌ ... لَكُم يَا قُرَيش والقَليب المُلَمَّم ...
Indeed, by my life, there was a lesson for you at Badr, O Quraysh, and at the well filled with corpses...

غَدَاة أتَى فِي الخَزْرَجيَّةِ عامِدًا ... إليكُم مُطيعًا للعَظيمِ المُكَرّم ...
On the morning he came, purposefully, in the Khazrajite (battle array), to you, obedient to the Mighty, the Generous...

مُعَانًا برُوح القُدْس يَنْكي عَدوه ... رَسُولا مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ حَقّا بِمَعْلم ...
Aided by the Holy Spirit, who inflicts defeat upon his enemy, a messenger from the Most Merciful, truly and clearly marked...

رَسُولا مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ يَتْلُو كِتابَهُ ... فَلَمّا أنارَ الحَقّ لَمْ يَتَلعْثَم ...
A messenger from the Most Merciful, reciting His Book; and when the truth shone forth, he did not falter...

أرَى أمْرَهُ يَزْدَادُ فِي كُلّ مَوْطن ... عُلُوّا لأمرْ حَمَّه اللهُ مُحْكَم [[انظر: السيرة النبوية لابن هشام (٢/١٩٥) .]]
I see his affair increasing in every situation, in exaltation, by a matter God has decreed and made firm. [See: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (2/195).]

وَقَدْ أَوْرَدَ ابْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ، هاهنا أَشْعَارًا كَثِيرَةً، فِيهَا آدَابٌ وَمَوَاعِظُ وَحِكَمٌ، وَتَفَاصِيلُ لِلْقِصَّةِ، تَرَكْنَا بَاقِيهَا اخْتِصَارًا وَاكْتِفَاءً بِمَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ، وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ وَالْمِنَّةُ.
Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, cited here many verses, containing courtesies, admonitions and wisdom, and details of the story. We have left out the remainder for brevity and being content with what we have mentioned. To God belongs all praise and grace.

قَالَ ابْنُ إِسْحَاقَ: كَانَتْ وَقْعَةُ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ بَعْدَ وَقْعَةِ أُحُدٍ وَبَعْدَ بِئْرِ مَعُونَةَ. وَحَكَى الْبُخَارِيُّ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: كَانَتْ وَقْعَةُ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ بَعْدَ بَدْرٍ بِسِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ [[صحيح البخاري (٧/٣٢٩) "فتح".]] .
Ibn Ishaq said: The incident of Banu al-Nadir occurred after the Battle of Uhud and after the well of Ma'una. Al-Bukhari related, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, that he said: The incident of Banu al-Nadir occurred six months after Badr. [Sahih al-Bukhari (7/329), Fath.]

**Commentary on Surah al-Hashr**

[It was also said by Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat Bani an-Nadir"] [[Addition from A.]]. It is a Medinan surah.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?" He said: "It was revealed concerning Bani an-Nadir." Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it by another route, from Hushaym, with the same chain [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4882, and Sahih Muslim, no. 3031.]]. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?" He said: "Say: Surat an-Nadir" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4883.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

He, exalted is He, informs that everything in the heavens and everything on the earth glorifies Him, extols Him, sanctifies Him, prays to Him, and affirms His oneness [[In M: "wahdahu" (alone).]], as in His saying: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. There is not a thing but that it glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra: 44]. His saying ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ means: the Unassailable in His dominion, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His decree and His legislation.

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book﴾ refers to the Jews of Bani an-Nadir. This was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, az-Zuhri, and others. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, he made a truce with them and gave them a covenant and a guarantee that he would not fight them and they would not fight him. Then they broke the covenant that was between them and him, so Allah brought upon them His might, which cannot be repelled, and sent down upon them His decree, which cannot be averted. The Prophet ﷺ then exiled them and expelled them from their fortified strongholds, which the Muslims had not expected to conquer, and they themselves thought that these would protect them from the might of Allah. But they availed them nothing against Allah, and there came upon them what they had not imagined. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them away and expelled them from Medina. A group of them went to Adhruʿat in the uplands of Syria, which is the land of the gathering and the assembling, and another group went to Khaybar. He had settled them there on the condition that they could take whatever their camels could carry. They would ruin what was in their houses of movable items that could be carried with them. Therefore He said: ﴿They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of insight﴾, that is: reflect upon the outcome of those who opposed the command of Allah, opposed His Messenger, and denied His Book, and how the painful punishment that He reserves for them in the Hereafter, together with the humiliating might that befalls them in this world, will come upon them.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Dawud and Sufyan narrated to us; 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, that the disbelieving Quraysh wrote to Ibn Ubayy and those with him who worshipped idols from the Aws and the Khazraj, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Medina before the Battle of Badr: "You have sheltered our companion, and we swear by Allah that we will certainly fight him, or you will expel him, or we will all march against you until we kill your fighting men and take your women captive." When this reached 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those with him among the idol-worshippers, they gathered to fight the Prophet ﷺ. When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he came to them and said: "The threat of Quraysh has reached you in its extremity. Their scheming against you is no more than what they wish to scheme against themselves. Do you wish to fight your own sons and brothers?" When they heard this from the Prophet ﷺ, they dispersed. This reached the disbelieving Quraysh, and after the Battle of Badr the disbelieving Quraysh wrote to the Jews: "You are the people of the ring-shaped fortifications and the strongholds, and you must fight alongside our companion, or we will do such-and-such. Nothing will stand between us and the ornaments of your women," meaning the anklets. When their letter reached the Prophet ﷺ, Bani an-Nadir gathered to act treacherously. They sent to the Prophet ﷺ: "Come out to us with thirty men of your companions, and thirty of our rabbis will come out, so that we may meet at a neutral place and they will hear from you. If they believe you and have faith in you, we will have faith in you too." When the next day came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them with the battalions and besieged them. He said to them: "By Allah, you will not be secure with me except under a covenant that you pledge to me." They refused to give him a covenant, so he fought them that day. Then the following day he went with the battalions against Bani Qurayzah and left Bani an-Nadir, and he called them to make a covenant with him, and they made a covenant, so he turned away from them. Then he went with the battalions against Bani an-Nadir and fought them until they agreed to leave. So Bani an-Nadir departed, taking with them what their camels could carry of their goods, the doors of their houses, and their timber. The date palms of Bani an-Nadir belonged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone, which Allah had given him and specially assigned to him. So He said: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not press forward against it with horse or camel﴾, meaning: without fighting. The Prophet ﷺ gave most of it to the Emigrants, dividing it among them, and he gave a share to two men of the Ansar who were in need, and no one else of the Ansar was given a share. What remained of it was the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which was in the hands of the family of Fatimah [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3004.]].

We shall mention a summary of the Battle of Bani an-Nadir in brief. And in Allah is the help sought.

The cause of it, as mentioned by the scholars of the campaigns and biographies, was that when the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Bi'r Ma'unah were killed, and they were seventy, only 'Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri escaped. On his way back to Medina he killed two men from Bani 'Amir, and they had a covenant and a safe-conduct from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which 'Amr did not know about. When he returned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed, and he said to him: "You have killed two men, and I will certainly pay their blood-money." There was an alliance and a covenant between Bani an-Nadir and Bani 'Amir. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Bani an-Nadir seeking their help in paying the blood-money for those two men. The dwellings of Bani an-Nadir were outside Medina, a few miles away to its east.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in his book, the Sirah: Then the Messenger of Allah went out to Bani an-Nadir, seeking their help in paying the blood-money for the two slain men from Bani 'Amir, whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri had killed, because of the protection that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had granted them, as Yazid ibn Ruman related to me. There was a pact and an alliance between Bani an-Nadir and Bani 'Amir. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them seeking their help in paying the blood-money for those two slain men, they said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, we will help you in what you wish, regarding what you have sought our help for." Then some of them withdrew to speak privately with one another, and they said: "You will never find the man in a situation like this, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is beside a wall of their houses. Who will climb onto this house and drop a stone on him, so that he will rid us of him?" 'Amr ibn Jihash ibn Ka'b, one of them, volunteered for this and said: "I will do it." He climbed up to drop a stone on him as he had said, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was with a group of his companions, among them Abu Bakr, 'Umar, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them. Then the news came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from heaven of what the people intended, so he stood up and went back toward Medina. When the Prophet ﷺ was delayed, his companions rose to look for him, and they met a man coming from Medina and asked him about him. He said: "I saw him entering Medina." So the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came until they reached him, and he told them what had happened, that the Jews had intended treachery against him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered them to prepare for war against them and to march against them. Then he set out until he arrived at them, and they took refuge from him in their fortresses. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the palm trees to be cut down and burned. They called out to him: "O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption and condemn those who committed it. What is the matter with cutting down and burning the palm trees?"

A group from Bani 'Awf ibn al-Khazraj, among them 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi'ah, Malik ibn Abi Qawqal, Suwayd, and Da'is, had sent to Bani an-Nadir: "Hold firm and defend yourselves, for we will not abandon you. If you are fought, we will fight alongside you, and if you are expelled, we will go out with you." They awaited that support from them, but they did not do so. Allah cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to exile them and to spare their lives, on the condition that they could take whatever their camels could carry of their property, except for the ring-shaped armour. He agreed, and they took from their property whatever the camels could carry. A man among them would dismantle his house from the frame of its door, place it on the back of his camel, and set off with it. Some of them went to Khaybar, and some of them went to Syria, and they left their property to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so it belonged to the Messenger of Allah alone, and he would place it wherever he willed. He divided it among the first Emigrants, to the exclusion of the Ansar, except that Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah mentioned their poverty, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave to them.

He said: None of Bani an-Nadir was spared except two men: Yamin ibn 'Umayr ibn Ka'b ibn 'Amr ibn Jihash, and Abu Sa'd ibn Wahb. They both embraced Islam, retaining their property, and so they secured it.

Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Yamin narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Yamin: "Did you not see what I suffered from your cousin, and what they intended against me?" Yamin ibn 'Umayr then offered a reward to a man on condition that he kill 'Amr ibn Jihash, and he killed him, as they allege.

Ibn Ishaq said: The Surah of al-Hashr was revealed in its entirety concerning Bani an-Nadir [[See: as-Sirah an-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (2/190–192) and Tafsir al-Tabari (28/21).]].

Thus Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Ibn Ishaq, in similar terms to what has preceded.

So His saying ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book﴾ refers to Bani an-Nadir, ﴿from their homes at the first gathering﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us; Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever doubts that the land of the gathering is here, meaning Syria, let him recite this verse: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Leave." They said: "To where?" He said: "To the land of the gathering."

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ exiled Bani an-Nadir, he said: "This is the first gathering, and I am following in its trail."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, with the same wording [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/20). Ibn Sa'd also narrated it in at-Tabaqat (2/42) from Hawdhah ibn Khalifah, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, and it is mursal.]].

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 59, verses 1–5 (part 2 of 3):

And His saying: ﴿You did not think that they would leave﴾, meaning: during the period of your siege of them, and its brevity, which was six days, despite the strength of their fortresses and their defences. For this reason He said: ﴿And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah, but Allah came at them from where they did not expect﴾, meaning: there came to them a command from Allah that had never occurred to them, as He said in another verse: ﴿Those before them had already schemed, so Allah came at their structures from the foundations, and the roof fell down on them from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive﴾ [An-Nahl: 26].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾, meaning: fear, panic and dismay. How could they not experience that, when the one who was supported with terror (ﷺ) had besieged them from a distance of a month's journey? May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾. The interpretation of Ibn Ishaq regarding this has already been mentioned: it is the dismantling of what they had admired of their roofs and doors, and carrying them on camels. Likewise said 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fight them, and whenever he gained control over an alley or a house, he would demolish its walls so that the space would be wide enough for fighting. The Jews, whenever they occupied a place or overpowered an alley or a house, would dig through its back walls, then fortify and barricade them. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿So take warning, O you with insight﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Had Allah not decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world﴾, meaning: had Allah not decreed for them this exile, which is their expulsion from their homes and their wealth, they would have had another punishment from Allah, namely killing, captivity and the like. This was said by al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, and by al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, because Allah had decreed for them that He would punish them in the worldly abode, in addition to what He had prepared for them in the Hereafter of the punishment of the Fire of Hell.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to me, from al-Layth, from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, saying: Then came the event of the Banu al-Nadir, who were a group of the Jews, six months after the Battle of Badr. Their dwelling was in one part of Medina, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them until they came down to accept exile, and that they would have whatever wealth and goods the camels could carry, except the weapons (al-halqah), which is the arms. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) exiled them towards Syria. He said: The exile was that it had been prescribed for them in certain verses of the Torah, and they were from a tribe that had not been subjected to exile before what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given power over. And Allah sent down concerning them: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾ up to His saying ﴿and that He may disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾.

ʿIkrimah said: The exile (al-jala') is killing. In another narration from him: it is annihilation.

Qatadah said: The exile is the departure of people from one town to another town.

al-Dahhak said: He exiled them to Syria, and gave every three of them a camel and a water-skin. That is the exile.

The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Ahmad ibn Kamil al-Qadi informed us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-'Awfi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my paternal uncle, from my father, from my grandfather, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had besieged them until he reached every extremity with them, so they offered him what he desired from them. He made peace with them on the condition that he would spare their lives, that he would expel them from their land, their homes and their homelands, and that he would send them to Adhri'at in Syria, and he gave every three of them a camel and a water-skin. The exile (al-jala') is their expulsion from their land to another land. [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi (3/359); its chain is a chain consisting entirely of weak narrators.]

It has also been narrated through Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri, from Ibrahim ibn Ja'far ibn Mahmud ibn Muhammad ibn Maslamah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Muhammad ibn Maslamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him to the Banu al-Nadir and ordered him to give them a respite of three nights for the exile. [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/360).]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: a decisive, binding matter from which they cannot escape.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: Allah did that to them and gave power over them to His Messenger and His believing servants only because they opposed Allah and His Messenger, and denied what Allah had sent down to His earlier messengers regarding the good news of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they recognised that just as they recognise their own sons. Then He said: ﴿And whoever opposes Allah, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾. Al-liyah: a type of date, and it is good quality.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: It is what differs from al-'ajwah and al-barni among dates.

Many of the exegetes said: al-liynah is the varieties of dates other than al-'ajwah.

Ibn Jarir said: It is the whole of the palm trees, and he attributed to Mujahid: and it is also al-Buwayrah. That is because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them, he ordered that their palm trees be cut down, as a humiliation to them, and as intimidation and terror for their hearts. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Yazid ibn Ruman, Qatadah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: [Then the Banu al-Nadir] said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): You forbid corruption, so why do you order the cutting of trees? So Allah sent down this noble verse: meaning, whatever you cut down and whatever trees you left, all of it is by the permission of Allah, His will, His power, and His pleasure. In it is a blow against the enemy, disgrace for them, and the humbling of their noses.

Mujahid said: Some of the emigrants forbade others from cutting palm trees, and they said: They are only the spoils of the Muslims. So the Qur'an was revealed confirming those who forbade cutting them, and permitting those who cut them from sin, and the cutting and leaving were by His permission. This has also been narrated in a raised (marfu') form. al-Nasa'i said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, from 'Affan, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, Habib ibn Abi 'Amrah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾, he said: They were bringing them down from their fortresses, and they ordered the cutting of palm trees, so this troubled their hearts. The Muslims said: We cut some and left some, so let us ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Is there a reward for us in what we cut? And is there a sin upon us for what we left? So Allah sent down: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down﴾. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11574).]

The hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, Hafs narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Jabir, and from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: He (ﷺ) permitted them to cut palm trees, then he tightened the restriction on them, so they asked the Prophet (ﷺ): O Messenger of Allah, is there a sin upon us for what we cut? Or is there a burden upon us for what we left? So Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah﴾. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (4/135), in which is Sufyan ibn Waki', who is weak. Note: the narration of Sulayman ibn Musa from Jabir I have not found in the printed Musnad of Abu Ya'la, so it may have fallen out.]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut down the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir and burned them.

The two authors of the Sahihs also narrated it through Musa ibn 'Uqbah, with similar wording. [Musnad (2/7); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2021); Sahih Muslim no. (1746).] The wording of al-Bukhari, through 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: al-Nadir and Quraydah fought, so he exiled the Banu al-Nadir and kept Quraydah, and was gracious to them, until Quraydah fought, so he killed their men, took their women, children and wealth and divided them among the Muslims, except for some of them who joined the Prophet (ﷺ), and he granted them safety and they embraced Islam. He also exiled all the Jews of Medina: the Banu Qaynuqa', who were the kin of 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, the Jews of the Banu Harithah, and all the Jews in Medina.

Also in both of them, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir and cut them down, and that is al-Buwayrah. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down concerning it: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of Allah, and so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4884); Sahih Muslim no. (1746).]

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, has, through the narration of Juwayriyah ibn Asma' from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir. [In some manuscripts: "the palm trees of the Banu al-Nadir and cut al-Buwayrah"; the phrase "cut al-Buwayrah" is not established in al-Bukhari, and it appears to be an error of a copyist.] And about it Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

The burning at al-Buwayrah, spreading far and wide, was made light in the eyes of the nobles of the Banu Lu'ayy...

Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith replied, saying:

May Allah perpetuate that deed of yours, and the blaze that burned in its surroundings...
You will know which of us will have a delight in it, and you will know which of our lands is Nadir...

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it, and Ibn Ishaq did not mention it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Ka'b ibn Malik said, recalling the exile of the Banu al-Nadir and the killing of Ibn al-Ashraf:

Indeed they were disgraced by their treachery, the Hubur... [the verses as recorded in the source]

أَهْلِي فدَاءٌ لِامْرِئٍ غَير هَالك ... أحَلّ [[في أ: "أجلي".]] اليهودَ بالحَسِى [[في م، أ: "بالحس".]] المُزَنَّم ...
May my family be a ransom for a man who is not destroyed, who settled the Jews at al-Hasi al-Muzannam...

يَقيلُونَ فِي جَمْر الغَضاة وبُدّلُوا ... أهَيضبَ عُودًا بالوَدي المُكَمَّم ...
They take their midday rest on the embers of the ghada tree, and they were exchanged for a rain-drenched stick in the valley of al-Wadi al-Mukammam...

فَإِنْ يَكُ ظَني صَادقًا بمُحَمد ... يَرَوا خَيلَه بينَ الصِّلَا وَيَرمْرَم [[في أ: "بين الصفا وبزمزم".]]
So if my assumption about Muhammad is true, they will see his horses between al-Sila and Yarmaram [[In A: "between al-Safa and Zamzam".]]...

يَؤمّ بِهَا عَمرو بنُ بُهثَةَ إنَّهُمْ ... عَدُو ما حَيّ صَديق كمُجْرم ...
Amr ibn Buhtha leads them, for they are an enemy, as long as any tribe is a friend like a criminal...

عَلَيهنّ أبطالُ مَساعيرُ فِي الوَغَى ... يَهُزّونَ أطرافَ الوَشيج المُقَوّم ...
Upon them are heroes who kindle the flames of battle, brandishing the tips of straight, well-made spear shafts...

وكُلّ رَقيق الشَّفرتَين مُهَنَّدٍ ... تُورثْنَ مِنْ أزْمان عَادٍ وَجُرْهُمِ ...
And every thin-edged, Indian-made sword, inherited from the times of ʿAd and Jurhum...

فَمَن مُبلغٌ عَني قُرَيشًا رسَالة ... فَهَلْ بَعدَهُم فِي المجْد مِنْ مُتَكرّم ...
Who will convey from me a message to Quraysh? Is there, after them, anyone in glory who is more noble?

بِأَنَّ أخاكمُ فاعلَمنّ مُحَمَّدًا ... تَليدُ النَّدى بينَ الحَجُون وزَمْزَم ...
That your brother, Muhammad, know well, is the inherited generosity between al-Hajun and Zamzam...

فَدينُوا لَهُ بِالْحَقِّ تَجْسُمْ أمُورُكم ... وتَسْمُوا منَ الدنْيا إِلَى كُل مُعْظَم ...
So submit to him in truth, and your affairs will be set right, and you will rise from this world to every exalted height...

نَبِيٌّ تلافَته منَ اللَّهِ رَحَمةٌ ... وَلَا تَسْألُوهُ أمْرَ غَيب مُرَجَّم ...
He is a Prophet whom mercy from God has embraced; and do not ask him about a hidden matter that is conjectured...

فَقَدْ كانَ فِي بَدْر لَعَمْري عِبرَةٌ ... لَكُم يَا قُرَيش والقَليب المُلَمَّم ...
Indeed, by my life, there was a lesson for you at Badr, O Quraysh, and at the well filled with corpses...

غَدَاة أتَى فِي الخَزْرَجيَّةِ عامِدًا ... إليكُم مُطيعًا للعَظيمِ المُكَرّم ...
On the morning he came, purposefully, in the Khazrajite (battle array), to you, obedient to the Mighty, the Generous...

مُعَانًا برُوح القُدْس يَنْكي عَدوه ... رَسُولا مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ حَقّا بِمَعْلم ...
Aided by the Holy Spirit, who inflicts defeat upon his enemy, a messenger from the Most Merciful, truly and clearly marked...

رَسُولا مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ يَتْلُو كِتابَهُ ... فَلَمّا أنارَ الحَقّ لَمْ يَتَلعْثَم ...
A messenger from the Most Merciful, reciting His Book; and when the truth shone forth, he did not falter...

أرَى أمْرَهُ يَزْدَادُ فِي كُلّ مَوْطن ... عُلُوّا لأمرْ حَمَّه اللهُ مُحْكَم [[انظر: السيرة النبوية لابن هشام (٢/١٩٥) .]]
I see his affair increasing in every situation, in exaltation, by a matter God has decreed and made firm. [See: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (2/195).]

وَقَدْ أَوْرَدَ ابْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ، هاهنا أَشْعَارًا كَثِيرَةً، فِيهَا آدَابٌ وَمَوَاعِظُ وَحِكَمٌ، وَتَفَاصِيلُ لِلْقِصَّةِ، تَرَكْنَا بَاقِيهَا اخْتِصَارًا وَاكْتِفَاءً بِمَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ، وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ وَالْمِنَّةُ.
Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, cited here many verses, containing courtesies, admonitions and wisdom, and details of the story. We have left out the remainder for brevity and being content with what we have mentioned. To God belongs all praise and grace.

قَالَ ابْنُ إِسْحَاقَ: كَانَتْ وَقْعَةُ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ بَعْدَ وَقْعَةِ أُحُدٍ وَبَعْدَ بِئْرِ مَعُونَةَ. وَحَكَى الْبُخَارِيُّ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: كَانَتْ وَقْعَةُ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ بَعْدَ بَدْرٍ بِسِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ [[صحيح البخاري (٧/٣٢٩) "فتح".]] .
Ibn Ishaq said: The incident of Banu al-Nadir occurred after the Battle of Uhud and after the well of Ma'una. Al-Bukhari related, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, that he said: The incident of Banu al-Nadir occurred six months after Badr. [Sahih al-Bukhari (7/329), Fath.]

Ibn Kathir said, explaining what al-fay' (the property gained from the enemy without fighting) is, what its nature is, and what its ruling is:

Al-fay' is every property taken from the disbelievers without fighting and without the use of horses or camels, such as the property of the Banu al-Nadir here. For they are among those things over which the Muslims did not charge with horses or camels; that is, they did not fight the enemy over it by single combat or by close engagement. Rather, those people came down (from their fortresses) out of the terror that Allah cast into their hearts because of the awe of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah granted it (as fay') to His Messenger, and for this reason he disposed of it as he willed. He allotted it to the Muslims in the channels of righteousness and the public interests that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, mentioned in these verses, when He said: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them﴾, meaning from the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿you did not charge for it with horses or camels﴾, meaning camels, ﴿but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. That is, He is Competent, not overcome and not resisted, but rather He is the Subduer of everything.

Then He said: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, meaning all the towns that are conquered in this manner. Their ruling is the ruling of the property of the Banu al-Nadir. For this reason He said: ﴿for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy﴾ up to the end of it, and what follows it. These are the expenditure channels and the purposes of the property of al-fay'.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr and Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The property of the Banu al-Nadir was among what Allah restored to His Messenger, of what the Muslims had not charged for with horses or camels. So it was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would spend on his family from it the provision of his year — and he said on one occasion: the sustenance of his year — and whatever remained he placed in horses and weapons in the way of Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

Thus Ahmad transmitted it here in abridged form. The group (of compilers) transmitted it in their books — except Ibn Majah — from the hadith of Sufyan, from Amr ibn Dinar, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording.[[Musnad (1/25); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4885); Sahih Muslim no. (1757); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2965); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1719); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11575).]] We have narrated it in a longer form. Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris narrated to us — the meaning is one — they said: Bishr ibn Umar al-Zahrani narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Malik ibn Aws, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, sent for me when the day had grown bright. I came to him and found him sitting on a bed without a mattress, with his cushions beneath him. When I entered upon him he said: "O Malik, the people of some households from your tribe have come to us, and I have ordered something concerning them, so divide it among them." I said: "Would you order someone other than me to do that?" He said: "Take it." Then Yarfa came and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, would you like to see Uthman ibn Affan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas?" He said: "Yes." So he permitted them and they entered. Then Yarfa came again and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, would you like to see al-Abbas and Ali?" He said: "Yes." So he permitted them and they entered. Al-Abbas said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this one" — meaning Ali. Some of them said: "Yes indeed, O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve them." Malik ibn Aws said: "It seemed to me that they had brought those people forward for that purpose." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Be patient." Then he turned to that group and said: "I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity'?" They said: "Yes." Then he turned to Ali and al-Abbas and said: "I adjure you both by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you both know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity'?" They both said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed Allah specially favoured His Messenger with a particular thing which He did not favour any of the people with. He said: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them — you did not charge for it with horses or camels, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. So Allah restored to His Messenger the property of the Banu al-Nadir. By Allah, he did not keep it to himself over you, nor did he take it to the exclusion of you. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would take from it the provision of a year — or: his provision and his family's provision for a year — and place what remained as a common fund for the wealth." Then he turned again to that group and said: "I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you know this?" They said: "Yes." Then he turned to Ali and al-Abbas and said: "I adjure you both by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you both know this?" They said: "Yes." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, Abu Bakr said: "I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah." You two came to Abu Bakr seeking your inheritance — you, al-Abbas, seeking your nephew's inheritance, and this one seeking his wife's inheritance from her father. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity.'" And Allah knows that he was truthful, pious, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. So Abu Bakr took charge of it. When he died, I said: "I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah and the guardian of Abu Bakr," and I managed it for as long as Allah willed that I manage it. Then you two came, and your affair was one and the same, and you asked me for it. I said: "If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you bind yourselves by the covenant of Allah to manage it in the way the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) managed it." You took it from me on that basis, and then you came to me to judge between you in some other way. By Allah, I will not judge between you otherwise until the Hour comes. If you are unable to manage it, then return it to me.

They narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same wording.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2963); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3094); Sahih Muslim no. (1757); Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/136); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1610).]] Imam Ahmad also said:

Ariim and Affan narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us: I heard my father say: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): A man would allot to him some of his property, some date palms, or as Allah willed, until Qurayzah and al-Nadir were conquered for him. He said: Then he began to take them back afterwards. He said: My family ordered me to go to the Prophet (ﷺ) and ask him for what his family had given him, or part of it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) had given it to Umm Ayman, or as Allah willed. He said: So I asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he gave them to me. Then Umm Ayman came, put the garment around my neck, and began to say: "No, by Allah, by whom there is no god but He, he will not give them to you, when he has given them to me" — or as she said. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For you is such-and-such." He said: She kept saying: "No, by Allah." He said: He kept saying: "For you is such-and-such." He said: She kept saying: "No, by Allah." He said: "He keeps saying: For you is such-and-such." He said: Until he gave her — I think he said: ten times, or he said: about ten times its amount — or as he said.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it through several routes from Mu'tamir, with the same wording.[[Musnad (3/219); Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (3128, 4030, 4120); Sahih Muslim no. (1771).]]

* *

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan al-Awfi, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Masruq, who said: A woman came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "It has reached me that you forbid the tattooed woman and the one who has hair added." Is this something you found in the Book of Allah, or from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: "Yes, something I found in the Book of Allah and from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "By Allah, I have examined what is between the two covers of the Mushaf, and I did not find in it what you say!" He said: "Did you not find in it: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾?" She said: "Yes." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbid the one who has hair added, the tattooed woman, and the one who plucks her eyebrows." She said: "Perhaps it is among some of your family." He said: "Go in and look." She went in and looked, then came out and said: "I saw nothing wrong." Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, [from Ibrahim] from Alqamah, from Abd Allah — that is Ibn Mas'ud — who said: Allah curses the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck their eyebrows, and those who file their teeth for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah, mighty and majestic is He. He said: It reached a woman in the household called "Umm Ya'qub," so she came to him and said: "It has reached me that you said such-and-such." He said: "Why should I not curse one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, and it is in the Book of Allah?" She said: "I read what is between its two covers and did not find it." He said: "If you have read it, then you have found it. Did you not read: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾?" She said: "Yes." He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade it." She said: "[I] think your household does it." He said: "Go and look."

She went and saw nothing of what she sought, so she came and said: "I saw nothing." He said: "If it were so, she would not have been with us."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri.[[Musnad (1/433); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4887); Sahih Muslim no. (2125).]]

Al-Nasa'i said: Ahmad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Mansur ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, that they both testified concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he forbade the dubba', the hantam, the naqir, and the muzaffat. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾.[[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11578).]]

* *

His words: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾ mean: Fear Him by carrying out His commands and abandoning what He prohibits, for He is severe in punishment toward whoever disobeys Him, opposes His command and refuses it, and commits what He has forbidden and prohibited.

Ibn Kathir said, explaining what al-fay' (the property gained from the enemy without fighting) is, what its nature is, and what its ruling is:

Al-fay' is every property taken from the disbelievers without fighting and without the use of horses or camels, such as the property of the Banu al-Nadir here. For they are among those things over which the Muslims did not charge with horses or camels; that is, they did not fight the enemy over it by single combat or by close engagement. Rather, those people came down (from their fortresses) out of the terror that Allah cast into their hearts because of the awe of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah granted it (as fay') to His Messenger, and for this reason he disposed of it as he willed. He allotted it to the Muslims in the channels of righteousness and the public interests that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, mentioned in these verses, when He said: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them﴾, meaning from the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿you did not charge for it with horses or camels﴾, meaning camels, ﴿but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. That is, He is Competent, not overcome and not resisted, but rather He is the Subduer of everything.

Then He said: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, meaning all the towns that are conquered in this manner. Their ruling is the ruling of the property of the Banu al-Nadir. For this reason He said: ﴿for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy﴾ up to the end of it, and what follows it. These are the expenditure channels and the purposes of the property of al-fay'.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr and Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The property of the Banu al-Nadir was among what Allah restored to His Messenger, of what the Muslims had not charged for with horses or camels. So it was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would spend on his family from it the provision of his year — and he said on one occasion: the sustenance of his year — and whatever remained he placed in horses and weapons in the way of Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

Thus Ahmad transmitted it here in abridged form. The group (of compilers) transmitted it in their books — except Ibn Majah — from the hadith of Sufyan, from Amr ibn Dinar, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording.[[Musnad (1/25); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4885); Sahih Muslim no. (1757); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2965); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1719); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11575).]] We have narrated it in a longer form. Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris narrated to us — the meaning is one — they said: Bishr ibn Umar al-Zahrani narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Malik ibn Aws, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, sent for me when the day had grown bright. I came to him and found him sitting on a bed without a mattress, with his cushions beneath him. When I entered upon him he said: "O Malik, the people of some households from your tribe have come to us, and I have ordered something concerning them, so divide it among them." I said: "Would you order someone other than me to do that?" He said: "Take it." Then Yarfa came and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, would you like to see Uthman ibn Affan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas?" He said: "Yes." So he permitted them and they entered. Then Yarfa came again and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, would you like to see al-Abbas and Ali?" He said: "Yes." So he permitted them and they entered. Al-Abbas said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this one" — meaning Ali. Some of them said: "Yes indeed, O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve them." Malik ibn Aws said: "It seemed to me that they had brought those people forward for that purpose." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Be patient." Then he turned to that group and said: "I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity'?" They said: "Yes." Then he turned to Ali and al-Abbas and said: "I adjure you both by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you both know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity'?" They both said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed Allah specially favoured His Messenger with a particular thing which He did not favour any of the people with. He said: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them — you did not charge for it with horses or camels, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. So Allah restored to His Messenger the property of the Banu al-Nadir. By Allah, he did not keep it to himself over you, nor did he take it to the exclusion of you. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would take from it the provision of a year — or: his provision and his family's provision for a year — and place what remained as a common fund for the wealth." Then he turned again to that group and said: "I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you know this?" They said: "Yes." Then he turned to Ali and al-Abbas and said: "I adjure you both by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you both know this?" They said: "Yes." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, Abu Bakr said: "I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah." You two came to Abu Bakr seeking your inheritance — you, al-Abbas, seeking your nephew's inheritance, and this one seeking his wife's inheritance from her father. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity.'" And Allah knows that he was truthful, pious, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. So Abu Bakr took charge of it. When he died, I said: "I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah and the guardian of Abu Bakr," and I managed it for as long as Allah willed that I manage it. Then you two came, and your affair was one and the same, and you asked me for it. I said: "If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you bind yourselves by the covenant of Allah to manage it in the way the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) managed it." You took it from me on that basis, and then you came to me to judge between you in some other way. By Allah, I will not judge between you otherwise until the Hour comes. If you are unable to manage it, then return it to me.

They narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same wording.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2963); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3094); Sahih Muslim no. (1757); Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/136); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1610).]] Imam Ahmad also said:

Ariim and Affan narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us: I heard my father say: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): A man would allot to him some of his property, some date palms, or as Allah willed, until Qurayzah and al-Nadir were conquered for him. He said: Then he began to take them back afterwards. He said: My family ordered me to go to the Prophet (ﷺ) and ask him for what his family had given him, or part of it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) had given it to Umm Ayman, or as Allah willed. He said: So I asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he gave them to me. Then Umm Ayman came, put the garment around my neck, and began to say: "No, by Allah, by whom there is no god but He, he will not give them to you, when he has given them to me" — or as she said. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For you is such-and-such." He said: She kept saying: "No, by Allah." He said: He kept saying: "For you is such-and-such." He said: She kept saying: "No, by Allah." He said: "He keeps saying: For you is such-and-such." He said: Until he gave her — I think he said: ten times, or he said: about ten times its amount — or as he said.
