Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 59, verses 8–10 (Part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, says, describing the state of the poor who are entitled to the fay' (spoils that came to the Muslims without battle): ﴿Those who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure﴾. That is, they left their homes and opposed their people, seeking the good pleasure of Allah and His approval. ﴿And they support Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾. That is, these are the ones who confirmed their words by their deeds. These are the chiefs of the Muhajirun (the Emigrants).

Then He, exalted is He, said, praising the Ansar (the Helpers), and explaining their virtue, nobility, generosity, their freedom from envy, and their preference for others even when they themselves were in need. He said: ﴿And those who had settled [in the city] and [adopted] the faith before them﴾. That is, they dwelt in the abode of emigration (Madinah) before the Muhajirun arrived, and they believed before many of them did.

'Umar said: "I enjoin the Caliph after me [to honour] the first Muhajirun, that he recognise their right and preserve their dignity. And I enjoin him to [treat well] the Ansar, those who settled in the abode and in the faith before them: that he accept the good of their doers and overlook the wrong of their wrongdoers." Al-Bukhari narrated this here also.¹

* *

As for His saying ﴿They love those who emigrate to them﴾, that is, out of their generosity and nobility of soul, they love the Muhajirun and share their wealth with them.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Muhajirun said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have never seen people like those whom we came to: they were the best in sharing when little, and the best in giving when much. They relieved us of the burden and shared the benefit with us, so much so that we feared they would take all the reward!" He said: "No, so long as you praise them and supplicate Allah for them."

I have not found this in the books through this route.

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who heard Anas ibn Malik when he went out with him to al-Walid, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) invited the Ansar to grant them the land of al-Bahrayn. They said: "No, unless you grant our brothers among the Muhajirun the same." He said: "Since it is so, then be patient until you meet me, for after me you will surely encounter preference given to others (athara)."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route.

Al-Bukhari said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Ansar said: "Divide the date palms between us and our brothers." He said: "No." They said: "Then you suffice us the labour, and we share with you the fruit." They said: "We hear and we obey." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, without Muslim.

﴿And they find in their breasts no need for what they have been given﴾. That is, they find in themselves no envy of the Muhajirun for what Allah has favoured them with of status, nobility, precedence in mention, and rank.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "﴿They find in their breasts no need﴾ means envy."

"﴿For what they have been given﴾": Qatadah said: "That is, for what He gave their brothers." Ibn Zayd said likewise. Among what is cited as evidence for this meaning is what Imam Ahmad narrated, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "Now there will appear to you a man of the people of Paradise." A man of the Ansar appeared, his beard dripping from his ablution, holding his sandals in his left hand. The next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same, and that man appeared as he had the first time. On the third day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same again, and that man appeared in the same state as the first time. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As followed him and said: "I quarrelled with my father and swore that I would not enter upon him for three days. If you see fit to let me stay with you until those days pass, I will do so." He said: "Yes." Anas said: 'Abdullah used to relate that he spent those three nights with him and did not see him get up at all during the night, except that when he turned over on his bed he remembered Allah and magnified Him, until he rose for the Fajr prayer. 'Abdullah said: "Only I never heard him say anything but good. When the three nights had passed, I almost belittled his deeds, so I said: 'O servant of Allah, there was no anger or estrangement between me and my father, but I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say of you three times: "Now there will appear to you a man of the people of Paradise," and you appeared three times, so I wished to stay with you to see what your deeds were, so that I might follow them. But I did not see you doing much work. So what has brought you to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said?'" He said: "It is nothing but what you have seen." When I turned to leave, he called me back and said: "It is nothing but what you have seen, except that I do not find in myself any deceit toward any Muslim, nor do I envy anyone for a good that Allah has given him." 'Abdullah said: "This is what has brought you to that, and it is what cannot be borne."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Yawm wa al-Layla, from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar with it. This is a sound isnad according to the conditions of the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), but 'Uqayl and others narrated it from al-Zuhri, from a man, from Anas.² Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding His saying ﴿and they find in their breasts no need for what they have been given﴾: "That is, what they have been given means the Muhajirun." He said: "Some of the Ansar spoke about the wealth of Bani al-Nadir, so Allah rebuked them for that, saying: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur for it with horse or camel, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Your brothers have left their wealth and children and have come to you.' They said: 'Our wealth is shared among us in portions.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Or something other than that?' They said: 'And what is that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'They are a people who do not know how to work, so you suffice them and share the fruit with them.' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.'"³

* *

As for His saying ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾,⁴ that is, [they prefer] need, meaning: they give precedence to the needy over their own need, and they begin with people before themselves when they are in need of it.

It is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best charity is that given by one who has little." This station is higher than the state of those whom Allah describes in His saying: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾ [al-Insan: 8], and His saying: ﴿And gives wealth despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177].

For those give charity while they love what they give, and they may not have need of it or dire necessity for it. But these have preferred others over themselves despite their poverty and their need for what they spent. From this station, al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, gave away all his wealth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What have you left for your family?" He said: "I have left them Allah and His Messenger." Similar is the water that was offered to 'Ikrimah and his companions on the day of al-Yarmuk. Each of them ordered that it be given to his companion, while he was gravely wounded and in greatest need of water. Each one sent it to another, until it reached the third, and before it reached the third they had all died, none of them having drunk it. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased.

Al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, hunger has afflicted me." He sent to his wives, but found nothing with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Is there not a man who will host this one tonight? May Allah have mercy on him." A man from the Ansar stood up and said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He went to his household and said to his wife: "This is the guest of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); do not hold anything back from him." She said: "By Allah, I have nothing but the food of the children." He said: "When the children want supper, put them to sleep, come here, extinguish the lamp, and let us go hungry tonight." She did so. Then the man went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the morning, and he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was amazed, or laughed, at so-and-so and so-and-so." And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾.⁵

Al-Bukhari narrated it similarly in another place, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several routes, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, with similar wording.⁶ In a narration of Muslim, this Ansari is named Abu Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, those are the successful﴾, that is, whoever is safe from avarice has indeed succeeded and prospered.

Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra' informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection, and beware of avarice, for avarice destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was forbidden to them."

Muslim alone narrated it, from al-Qa'nabi, from Dawud ibn Qays, with it.⁷

Al-A'mash and Shu'bah said, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Zuhayr ibn al-Aqmar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection; beware of obscenity, for Allah does not love obscenity or the affectation of it; and beware of avarice, for it destroyed those before you: it commanded them to be unjust, and they were unjust; it commanded them to be wicked, and they were wicked; it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them."

Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated it through the route of Shu'bah, and al-Nasa'i through the route of al-A'mash, both from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with it.⁸

Al-Layth said, from Yazid [ibn al-Had], from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Safwan ibn Abi Yazid, from al-Qa'qa' ibn al-Lijlaj, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Dust gathered in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell will never gather in the belly of a servant, and avarice and faith will never gather in the heart of a servant."⁹

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 59, verses 8–10 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, who said: A man came to 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud) and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, I fear that I may have perished." He asked him, "And what is that?" He said: "I heard Allah say: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess (shuhh) of his own soul, it is those who are the successful﴾, and I am a stingy man. I can hardly bring myself to let anything out of my hand!" 'Abd Allah said: "That is not the stinginess (shuhh) that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an. The stinginess that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an is that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. What you describe is miserliness (bukhl), and miserliness is a wretched thing." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (28/29) through the chain of Jami'.]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Tariq ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi, who said: "I was circumambulating the House (the Ka'bah), and I saw a man saying: 'O Allah, protect me from the stinginess of my soul,' and he would not add anything to that. I said to him, and he said: 'If I am protected from the stinginess of my soul, I will not steal, I will not commit adultery, and I will not do such-and-such.'" And behold, the man was 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with him. [Narrated by Ibn Jarir.]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, Mujam' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Yazid ibn Jariyah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Free from stinginess is the one who pays the zakah, hospitably receives the guest, and gives in times of calamity." [Tafsir al-Tabari (28/29). Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (10842), through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. It is also narrated in a mursal form: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/188) through 'Amr ibn Yahya and Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, and Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat (4/202) through Ibn al-Mubarak, all of them from Mujam' ibn Yahya, from his paternal uncle, in mursal form.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment (ghill) toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾ These are the third category of those whose poor are entitled to the fay' (spoils obtained without battle) wealth. They are the Emigrants, then the Helpers, then the Successors (tabi'un) who follow them in excellence. As He said in the verse of Bara'ah: ﴿And the foremost early ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in excellence—Allah is pleased with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100]. Those who follow them in excellence are those who follow their good deeds and their beautiful qualities, and who invoke Allah for them, both in private and in public. Therefore He said in this noble verse: ﴿And those who came after them say﴾, meaning, saying: ﴿"Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment (ghill)"﴾, meaning, hatred and envy, ﴿"toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾

How excellent is what Imam Malik derived from this noble verse: that the Rafidi (a Shi'i extremist) who curses the Companions (sahabah) has no share in the fay' wealth, because he does not possess the qualities that Allah praised in those people in their saying: ﴿"Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that she said: "They were commanded to seek forgiveness for them, but they reviled them!" Then I recited this verse: ﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith"﴾, to the end of the verse.

Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah said, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: "You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), but you reviled them. I heard your Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'This nation will not pass away until its last generation curses its first.'" [Narrated by al-Baghawi in Ma'alim al-Tanzil (8/08). It has a witness in Sahih Muslim, no. (3022), from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "O son of my sister, they were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), but they reviled them."']

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them—you did not spur for it with horses or camels﴾ (al-Zuhri said: 'Umar said: "This is specifically for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," the villages of Fadak and such-and-such) "and so what Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the villages belongs to Allah and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, and to the poor Emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their properties," ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith before them﴾, ﴿and those who came after them﴾. So this verse encompassed all people, and no Muslim is left without a right in it—he said: Ayyub said: "or a share"—except some of those whom your slaves possess." Thus Abu Dawud narrated it, and there is a break (inqita') in its chain. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2966).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: ﴿Indeed, the alms are for the poor and the needy﴾ until he reached ﴿Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60]. Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives [and the orphans and the needy]﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the villages﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor﴾, ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith﴾, ﴿and those who came after them﴾. Then he said: "This verse has encompassed the Muslims in general, and there is no one except that he has a right in it." Then he said: "If I live, the shepherd (al-ra'i) of Sana'a (Bas-ru Himyar) will come to receive his share from it, without his brow having sweated for it."

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 59, verses 8–10 (Part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, says, describing the state of the poor who are entitled to the fay' (spoils that came to the Muslims without battle): ﴿Those who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure﴾. That is, they left their homes and opposed their people, seeking the good pleasure of Allah and His approval. ﴿And they support Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾. That is, these are the ones who confirmed their words by their deeds. These are the chiefs of the Muhajirun (the Emigrants).

Then He, exalted is He, said, praising the Ansar (the Helpers), and explaining their virtue, nobility, generosity, their freedom from envy, and their preference for others even when they themselves were in need. He said: ﴿And those who had settled [in the city] and [adopted] the faith before them﴾. That is, they dwelt in the abode of emigration (Madinah) before the Muhajirun arrived, and they believed before many of them did.

'Umar said: "I enjoin the Caliph after me [to honour] the first Muhajirun, that he recognise their right and preserve their dignity. And I enjoin him to [treat well] the Ansar, those who settled in the abode and in the faith before them: that he accept the good of their doers and overlook the wrong of their wrongdoers." Al-Bukhari narrated this here also.¹

* *

As for His saying ﴿They love those who emigrate to them﴾, that is, out of their generosity and nobility of soul, they love the Muhajirun and share their wealth with them.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Muhajirun said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have never seen people like those whom we came to: they were the best in sharing when little, and the best in giving when much. They relieved us of the burden and shared the benefit with us, so much so that we feared they would take all the reward!" He said: "No, so long as you praise them and supplicate Allah for them."

I have not found this in the books through this route.

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who heard Anas ibn Malik when he went out with him to al-Walid, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) invited the Ansar to grant them the land of al-Bahrayn. They said: "No, unless you grant our brothers among the Muhajirun the same." He said: "Since it is so, then be patient until you meet me, for after me you will surely encounter preference given to others (athara)."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route.

Al-Bukhari said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Ansar said: "Divide the date palms between us and our brothers." He said: "No." They said: "Then you suffice us the labour, and we share with you the fruit." They said: "We hear and we obey." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, without Muslim.

﴿And they find in their breasts no need for what they have been given﴾. That is, they find in themselves no envy of the Muhajirun for what Allah has favoured them with of status, nobility, precedence in mention, and rank.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "﴿They find in their breasts no need﴾ means envy."

"﴿For what they have been given﴾": Qatadah said: "That is, for what He gave their brothers." Ibn Zayd said likewise. Among what is cited as evidence for this meaning is what Imam Ahmad narrated, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "Now there will appear to you a man of the people of Paradise." A man of the Ansar appeared, his beard dripping from his ablution, holding his sandals in his left hand. The next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same, and that man appeared as he had the first time. On the third day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same again, and that man appeared in the same state as the first time. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As followed him and said: "I quarrelled with my father and swore that I would not enter upon him for three days. If you see fit to let me stay with you until those days pass, I will do so." He said: "Yes." Anas said: 'Abdullah used to relate that he spent those three nights with him and did not see him get up at all during the night, except that when he turned over on his bed he remembered Allah and magnified Him, until he rose for the Fajr prayer. 'Abdullah said: "Only I never heard him say anything but good. When the three nights had passed, I almost belittled his deeds, so I said: 'O servant of Allah, there was no anger or estrangement between me and my father, but I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say of you three times: "Now there will appear to you a man of the people of Paradise," and you appeared three times, so I wished to stay with you to see what your deeds were, so that I might follow them. But I did not see you doing much work. So what has brought you to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said?'" He said: "It is nothing but what you have seen." When I turned to leave, he called me back and said: "It is nothing but what you have seen, except that I do not find in myself any deceit toward any Muslim, nor do I envy anyone for a good that Allah has given him." 'Abdullah said: "This is what has brought you to that, and it is what cannot be borne."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Yawm wa al-Layla, from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar with it. This is a sound isnad according to the conditions of the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), but 'Uqayl and others narrated it from al-Zuhri, from a man, from Anas.² Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding His saying ﴿and they find in their breasts no need for what they have been given﴾: "That is, what they have been given means the Muhajirun." He said: "Some of the Ansar spoke about the wealth of Bani al-Nadir, so Allah rebuked them for that, saying: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur for it with horse or camel, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Your brothers have left their wealth and children and have come to you.' They said: 'Our wealth is shared among us in portions.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Or something other than that?' They said: 'And what is that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'They are a people who do not know how to work, so you suffice them and share the fruit with them.' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.'"³

* *

As for His saying ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾,⁴ that is, [they prefer] need, meaning: they give precedence to the needy over their own need, and they begin with people before themselves when they are in need of it.

It is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best charity is that given by one who has little." This station is higher than the state of those whom Allah describes in His saying: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾ [al-Insan: 8], and His saying: ﴿And gives wealth despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177].

For those give charity while they love what they give, and they may not have need of it or dire necessity for it. But these have preferred others over themselves despite their poverty and their need for what they spent. From this station, al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, gave away all his wealth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What have you left for your family?" He said: "I have left them Allah and His Messenger." Similar is the water that was offered to 'Ikrimah and his companions on the day of al-Yarmuk. Each of them ordered that it be given to his companion, while he was gravely wounded and in greatest need of water. Each one sent it to another, until it reached the third, and before it reached the third they had all died, none of them having drunk it. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased.

Al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, hunger has afflicted me." He sent to his wives, but found nothing with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Is there not a man who will host this one tonight? May Allah have mercy on him." A man from the Ansar stood up and said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He went to his household and said to his wife: "This is the guest of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); do not hold anything back from him." She said: "By Allah, I have nothing but the food of the children." He said: "When the children want supper, put them to sleep, come here, extinguish the lamp, and let us go hungry tonight." She did so. Then the man went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the morning, and he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was amazed, or laughed, at so-and-so and so-and-so." And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾.⁵

Al-Bukhari narrated it similarly in another place, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several routes, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, with similar wording.⁶ In a narration of Muslim, this Ansari is named Abu Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, those are the successful﴾, that is, whoever is safe from avarice has indeed succeeded and prospered.

Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra' informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection, and beware of avarice, for avarice destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was forbidden to them."

Muslim alone narrated it, from al-Qa'nabi, from Dawud ibn Qays, with it.⁷

Al-A'mash and Shu'bah said, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Zuhayr ibn al-Aqmar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection; beware of obscenity, for Allah does not love obscenity or the affectation of it; and beware of avarice, for it destroyed those before you: it commanded them to be unjust, and they were unjust; it commanded them to be wicked, and they were wicked; it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them."

Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated it through the route of Shu'bah, and al-Nasa'i through the route of al-A'mash, both from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with it.⁸

Al-Layth said, from Yazid [ibn al-Had], from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Safwan ibn Abi Yazid, from al-Qa'qa' ibn al-Lijlaj, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Dust gathered in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell will never gather in the belly of a servant, and avarice and faith will never gather in the heart of a servant."⁹

I heard your Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'This nation will not pass away until its last generation curses its first.'" [Narrated by al-Baghawi in Ma'alim al-Tanzil (8/08). It has a witness in Sahih Muslim, no. (3022), from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "O son of my sister, they were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), but they reviled them."']

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them—you did not spur for it with horses or camels﴾ (al-Zuhri said: 'Umar said: "This is specifically for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," the villages of Fadak and such-and-such) "and so what Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the villages belongs to Allah and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, and to the poor Emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their properties," ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith before them﴾, ﴿and those who came after them﴾. So this verse encompassed all people, and no Muslim is left without a right in it—he said: Ayyub said: "or a share"—except some of those whom your slaves possess." Thus Abu Dawud narrated it, and there is a break (inqita') in its chain. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2966).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: ﴿Indeed, the alms are for the poor and the needy﴾ until he reached ﴿Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60]. Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives [and the orphans and the needy]﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the villages﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor﴾, ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith﴾, ﴿and those who came after them﴾. Then he said: "This verse has encompassed the Muslims in general, and there is no one except that he has a right in it." Then he said: "If I live, the shepherd (al-ra'i) of Sana'a (Bas-ru Himyar) will come to receive his share from it, without his brow having sweated for it."

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 59, verses 8–10 (Part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, says, describing the state of the poor who are entitled to the fay' (spoils that came to the Muslims without battle): ﴿Those who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure﴾. That is, they left their homes and opposed their people, seeking the good pleasure of Allah and His approval. ﴿And they support Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾. That is, these are the ones who confirmed their words by their deeds. These are the chiefs of the Muhajirun (the Emigrants).

Then He, exalted is He, said, praising the Ansar (the Helpers), and explaining their virtue, nobility, generosity, their freedom from envy, and their preference for others even when they themselves were in need. He said: ﴿And those who had settled [in the city] and [adopted] the faith before them﴾. That is, they dwelt in the abode of emigration (Madinah) before the Muhajirun arrived, and they believed before many of them did.

'Umar said: "I enjoin the Caliph after me [to honour] the first Muhajirun, that he recognise their right and preserve their dignity. And I enjoin him to [treat well] the Ansar, those who settled in the abode and in the faith before them: that he accept the good of their doers and overlook the wrong of their wrongdoers." Al-Bukhari narrated this here also.¹

* *

As for His saying ﴿They love those who emigrate to them﴾, that is, out of their generosity and nobility of soul, they love the Muhajirun and share their wealth with them.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Muhajirun said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have never seen people like those whom we came to: they were the best in sharing when little, and the best in giving when much. They relieved us of the burden and shared the benefit with us, so much so that we feared they would take all the reward!" He said: "No, so long as you praise them and supplicate Allah for them."

I have not found this in the books through this route.

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who heard Anas ibn Malik when he went out with him to al-Walid, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) invited the Ansar to grant them the land of al-Bahrayn. They said: "No, unless you grant our brothers among the Muhajirun the same." He said: "Since it is so, then be patient until you meet me, for after me you will surely encounter preference given to others (athara)."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route.

Al-Bukhari said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Ansar said: "Divide the date palms between us and our brothers." He said: "No." They said: "Then you suffice us the labour, and we share with you the fruit." They said: "We hear and we obey." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, without Muslim.

﴿And they find in their breasts no need for what they have been given﴾. That is, they find in themselves no envy of the Muhajirun for what Allah has favoured them with of status, nobility, precedence in mention, and rank.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "﴿They find in their breasts no need﴾ means envy."

"﴿For what they have been given﴾": Qatadah said: "That is, for what He gave their brothers." Ibn Zayd said likewise. Among what is cited as evidence for this meaning is what Imam Ahmad narrated, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "Now there will appear to you a man of the people of Paradise." A man of the Ansar appeared, his beard dripping from his ablution, holding his sandals in his left hand. The next day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same, and that man appeared as he had the first time. On the third day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same again, and that man appeared in the same state as the first time. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As followed him and said: "I quarrelled with my father and swore that I would not enter upon him for three days. If you see fit to let me stay with you until those days pass, I will do so." He said: "Yes." Anas said: 'Abdullah used to relate that he spent those three nights with him and did not see him get up at all during the night, except that when he turned over on his bed he remembered Allah and magnified Him, until he rose for the Fajr prayer. 'Abdullah said: "Only I never heard him say anything but good. When the three nights had passed, I almost belittled his deeds, so I said: 'O servant of Allah, there was no anger or estrangement between me and my father, but I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say of you three times: "Now there will appear to you a man of the people of Paradise," and you appeared three times, so I wished to stay with you to see what your deeds were, so that I might follow them. But I did not see you doing much work. So what has brought you to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said?'" He said: "It is nothing but what you have seen." When I turned to leave, he called me back and said: "It is nothing but what you have seen, except that I do not find in myself any deceit toward any Muslim, nor do I envy anyone for a good that Allah has given him." 'Abdullah said: "This is what has brought you to that, and it is what cannot be borne."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Yawm wa al-Layla, from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar with it. This is a sound isnad according to the conditions of the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), but 'Uqayl and others narrated it from al-Zuhri, from a man, from Anas.² Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding His saying ﴿and they find in their breasts no need for what they have been given﴾: "That is, what they have been given means the Muhajirun." He said: "Some of the Ansar spoke about the wealth of Bani al-Nadir, so Allah rebuked them for that, saying: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur for it with horse or camel, but Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Your brothers have left their wealth and children and have come to you.' They said: 'Our wealth is shared among us in portions.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Or something other than that?' They said: 'And what is that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'They are a people who do not know how to work, so you suffice them and share the fruit with them.' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.'"³

* *

As for His saying ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾,⁴ that is, [they prefer] need, meaning: they give precedence to the needy over their own need, and they begin with people before themselves when they are in need of it.

It is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best charity is that given by one who has little." This station is higher than the state of those whom Allah describes in His saying: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾ [al-Insan: 8], and His saying: ﴿And gives wealth despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177].

For those give charity while they love what they give, and they may not have need of it or dire necessity for it. But these have preferred others over themselves despite their poverty and their need for what they spent. From this station, al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, gave away all his wealth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What have you left for your family?" He said: "I have left them Allah and His Messenger." Similar is the water that was offered to 'Ikrimah and his companions on the day of al-Yarmuk. Each of them ordered that it be given to his companion, while he was gravely wounded and in greatest need of water. Each one sent it to another, until it reached the third, and before it reached the third they had all died, none of them having drunk it. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased.

Al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, hunger has afflicted me." He sent to his wives, but found nothing with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Is there not a man who will host this one tonight? May Allah have mercy on him." A man from the Ansar stood up and said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He went to his household and said to his wife: "This is the guest of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); do not hold anything back from him." She said: "By Allah, I have nothing but the food of the children." He said: "When the children want supper, put them to sleep, come here, extinguish the lamp, and let us go hungry tonight." She did so. Then the man went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the morning, and he said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was amazed, or laughed, at so-and-so and so-and-so." And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾.⁵

Al-Bukhari narrated it similarly in another place, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several routes, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, with similar wording.⁶ In a narration of Muslim, this Ansari is named Abu Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, those are the successful﴾, that is, whoever is safe from avarice has indeed succeeded and prospered.

Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra' informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection, and beware of avarice, for avarice destroyed those before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was forbidden to them."

Muslim alone narrated it, from al-Qa'nabi, from Dawud ibn Qays, with it.⁷

Al-A'mash and Shu'bah said, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Zuhayr ibn al-Aqmar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection; beware of obscenity, for Allah does not love obscenity or the affectation of it; and beware of avarice, for it destroyed those before you: it commanded them to be unjust, and they were unjust; it commanded them to be wicked, and they were wicked; it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them."

Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated it through the route of Shu'bah, and al-Nasa'i through the route of al-A'mash, both from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with it.⁸

Al-Layth said, from Yazid [ibn al-Had], from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Safwan ibn Abi Yazid, from al-Qa'qa' ibn al-Lijlaj, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Dust gathered in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell will never gather in the belly of a servant, and avarice and faith will never gather in the heart of a servant."⁹

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 59, verses 8–10 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, who said: A man came to 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud) and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, I fear that I may have perished." He asked him, "And what is that?" He said: "I heard Allah say: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess (shuhh) of his own soul, it is those who are the successful﴾, and I am a stingy man. I can hardly bring myself to let anything out of my hand!" 'Abd Allah said: "That is not the stinginess (shuhh) that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an. The stinginess that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an is that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. What you describe is miserliness (bukhl), and miserliness is a wretched thing." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (28/29) through the chain of Jami'.]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Tariq ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Hayyaj al-Asadi, who said: "I was circumambulating the House (the Ka'bah), and I saw a man saying: 'O Allah, protect me from the stinginess of my soul,' and he would not add anything to that. I said to him, and he said: 'If I am protected from the stinginess of my soul, I will not steal, I will not commit adultery, and I will not do such-and-such.'" And behold, the man was 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with him. [Narrated by Ibn Jarir.]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, Mujam' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Yazid ibn Jariyah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Free from stinginess is the one who pays the zakah, hospitably receives the guest, and gives in times of calamity." [Tafsir al-Tabari (28/29). Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. (10842), through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. It is also narrated in a mursal form: al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/188) through 'Amr ibn Yahya and Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, and Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat (4/202) through Ibn al-Mubarak, all of them from Mujam' ibn Yahya, from his paternal uncle, in mursal form.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment (ghill) toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾ These are the third category of those whose poor are entitled to the fay' (spoils obtained without battle) wealth. They are the Emigrants, then the Helpers, then the Successors (tabi'un) who follow them in excellence. As He said in the verse of Bara'ah: ﴿And the foremost early ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in excellence—Allah is pleased with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100]. Those who follow them in excellence are those who follow their good deeds and their beautiful qualities, and who invoke Allah for them, both in private and in public. Therefore He said in this noble verse: ﴿And those who came after them say﴾, meaning, saying: ﴿"Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment (ghill)"﴾, meaning, hatred and envy, ﴿"toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾

How excellent is what Imam Malik derived from this noble verse: that the Rafidi (a Shi'i extremist) who curses the Companions (sahabah) has no share in the fay' wealth, because he does not possess the qualities that Allah praised in those people in their saying: ﴿"Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that she said: "They were commanded to seek forgiveness for them, but they reviled them!" Then I recited this verse: ﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith"﴾, to the end of the verse.

Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah said, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: "You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), but you reviled them. I heard your Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'This nation will not pass away until its last generation curses its first.'" [Narrated by al-Baghawi in Ma'alim al-Tanzil (8/08). It has a witness in Sahih Muslim, no. (3022), from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "O son of my sister, they were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), but they reviled them."']

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them—you did not spur for it with horses or camels﴾ (al-Zuhri said: 'Umar said: "This is specifically for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," the villages of Fadak and such-and-such) "and so what Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the villages belongs to Allah and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, and to the poor Emigrants who were driven out of their homes and their properties," ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith before them﴾, ﴿and those who came after them﴾. So this verse encompassed all people, and no Muslim is left without a right in it—he said: Ayyub said: "or a share"—except some of those whom your slaves possess." Thus Abu Dawud narrated it, and there is a break (inqita') in its chain. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2966).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: ﴿Indeed, the alms are for the poor and the needy﴾ until he reached ﴿Knowing, Wise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60]. Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives [and the orphans and the needy]﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the villages﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor﴾, ﴿and those who settled in the abode and in faith﴾, ﴿and those who came after them﴾. Then he said: "This verse has encompassed the Muslims in general, and there is no one except that he has a right in it." Then he said: "If I live, the shepherd (al-ra'i) of Sana'a (Bas-ru Himyar) will come to receive his share from it, without his brow having sweated for it."

Allah, the Exalted, informs about the hypocrites, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, when they were sent to the Jews of Banu al-Nadir, promising them support from themselves. Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿Have you not considered those who played the hypocrite, saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture: "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." But Allah testifies that they are liars.﴾ That is, they are liars in what they promised them, either because they said to them a statement that they did not intend to fulfill, or because what they said did not come to pass. For this reason He says: ﴿And if they are fought, they will not support them. And if they support them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.﴾ That is, they will not fight alongside them. And ﴿if they support them﴾ means they fight alongside them. ﴿Then they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.﴾ This is a self-contained good news (for the believers).

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah.﴾ That is, they fear you more than they fear Allah. This is like His saying: ﴿And they fear people as they fear Allah or with even greater fear.﴾ [An-Nisa: 77]. For this reason He says: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

Then He says: ﴿They will not fight you all together except within fortified towns or from behind walls.﴾ That is, out of their cowardice and fear, they are unable to face the army of Islam in single combat or in direct confrontation, but rather (they fight) from within fortresses or from behind walls, under siege, so they fight in defense of themselves out of necessity.

Then He says: ﴿Their violence among themselves is intense.﴾ That is, their enmity among themselves is severe, as He said: ﴿and makes some of you taste the violence of others﴾ [Al-Anam: 65]. For this reason He says: ﴿You think they are united, but their hearts are divided.﴾ That is, you see them gathered together, so you think they are in harmony, while in truth they are in the utmost disagreement.

He (Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi) said: "That is, the People of the Scripture and the hypocrites: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾"

Then He says: ﴿Like those before them who had recently tasted the consequence of their affair, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ Mujahid, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "That is, like what befell the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Badr."

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Like those before them﴾ means the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa. This was also said by Qatadah and Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

This view is closer to the truth, for the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa had been expelled by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before this.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ That is, the likeness of these Jews in being deceived by those hypocrites who promised them support, and the hypocrites' saying to them: ﴿And if you are fought, we will surely support you.﴾ Then when the realities became clear and the siege and fighting bore down on them, the hypocrites abandoned them and left them to destruction. Their example in this is like the Shaytan, when he beautified disbelief for man, may Allah protect us, and when man entered into what he had beautified for him, the Shaytan disowned him and distanced himself, saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

Some of them have mentioned here a story of one of the worshippers of the Children of Israel, which is like an example of this parable. It is not the sole intended meaning of the parable, but rather it is one of many incidents similar to it. Ibn Jarir said:

Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us: Shuʿbah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Nahik say: I heard Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "A monk worshipped for sixty years, and Shaytan wanted him but was unable to overcome him. So he targeted a woman and made her insane, and she had brothers. He said to her brothers: 'Take this woman to this priest so that he may treat her.' They brought her to him, and he treated her, and she stayed with him. One day, while he was with her, he was attracted to her, so he approached her and she became pregnant. He then went to her and killed her. Then her brothers came, and Shaytan said to the monk: 'I am your companion. You have wearied me. I did this to you, so obey me and I will save you from what I have done to you. Prostrate to me one prostration.' So he prostrated to him. When he prostrated, (Shaytan) said: 'Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.' That is His saying: ﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man, 'Disbelieve.' But when he disbelieves, he says, 'Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.'﴾"

Ibn Jarir also said: Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Masʿudi narrated to me: my father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Aʿmash, from Umarah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abdullah ibn Masʿud, regarding this verse: ﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ He said: "There was a woman who tended sheep, and she had four brothers, and she used to take shelter at night at the cell of a monk. Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Hashr, verses 18–20:

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) early in the day. He said: Then a people came to him, barefoot, naked, wearing woolen cloaks (or abas), girded with swords, most of them from Mudar, nay, all of them from Mudar. The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed when he saw their poverty. He went in and came out again, then he commanded Bilal, who gave the adhan and iqamah. He prayed, then delivered a sermon and said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul﴾ until the end of the verse, ﴿indeed Allah is ever, over you, an Watcher﴾ [An-Nisa: 1]. And he recited the verse in al-Hashr: ﴿Let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾.

A man gave in charity from his dinar, from his dirham, from his garment, from a sa' of his wheat, from a sa' of his dates, until he said: 'Even with half a date.' Then a man from the Ansar came with a bag, his hand almost unable to carry it, rather it was unable to carry it. Then the people followed one another until I saw two heaps of food and clothing, until I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brightening as if it were gold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without anything being diminished from their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, without anything being diminished from their burdens.'"

Muslim alone narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, with a chain similar to this (Al-Musnad (4/358) and Sahih Muslim no. (1017)).

So His saying, ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾, is a command to have taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of Allah) of Him, and it includes doing what one has been commanded and abstaining from what one has been forbidden.

* *

His saying, ﴿Let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾, means: take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, and consider what you have stored up for yourselves of righteous deeds for the Day of your return and your presentation before your Lord. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ is a second emphasis. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ means: know that He is Knowing of all your deeds and your conditions, nothing of you is hidden from Him, and nothing of your affairs, great or small, is absent from Him.

And He said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾, meaning: do not forget the remembrance of Allah, lest He cause you to forget working for the good of your own souls that will benefit you on your return. Indeed, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. For this reason He said: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who have departed from the obedience of Allah, who will perish on the Day of Resurrection, who will be losers on the day of their return, as He said: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 9].

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Hawti narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Hariz ibn Uthman narrated to us, from Nu'aym ibn Namhah, who said: In the sermon of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) was: "Do you not know that you go forth and return for a known term? Whoever is able to fulfil his term while in the service of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, let him do so, and you will not attain that except through Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, a people made their terms for others, so Allah has forbidden you to be like them: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾. Where are those among your brothers whom you know? They have gone forth with what they sent ahead in the days of their predecessors, and they have departed with wretchedness and happiness. Where are the first tyrants who built cities and fortified them with walls? They have become beneath the rock and the wells. This is the Book of Allah, whose wonders do not perish, so seek illumination from it for a day of darkness, [and be illuminated by its light and clarification]. Indeed Allah praised Zakariyya and his household, saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, and they invoked Us in hope and fear, and they were humble before Us﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 90]. There is no good in speech not intended for the countenance of Allah, no good in wealth not spent in the cause of Allah, no good in one whose ignorance overcomes his forbearance, and no good in one who fears, regarding Allah, the blame of any blamer."

(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/60).)

This is a good chain (isnad), all of whose narrators are trustworthy (thiqat). The teacher of Hariz ibn Uthman, Nu'aym ibn Namhah, I do not know, neither by negation nor affirmation. However, Abu Dawud al-Sijistani ruled that all of Hariz's teachers are trustworthy. Witnesses (shawahid) to this sermon have been narrated through other channels. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal; the companions of Paradise – they are the attainers of success﴾, means (blank in manuscript) that these two groups are not equal in the judgment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is their judgment﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 21]. And He said: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer﴾ [Ghafir: 58]. He said: ﴿Shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth? Or shall We make the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28]. These and other verses indicate that Allah, glorified is He, honours the righteous and humiliates the wicked. For this reason He says here: ﴿The companions of Paradise are the attainers of success﴾, meaning those who are saved, those who are safe from the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Hashr, verses 18–20:

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) early in the day. He said: Then a people came to him, barefoot, naked, wearing woolen cloaks (or abas), girded with swords, most of them from Mudar, nay, all of them from Mudar. The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed when he saw their poverty. He went in and came out again, then he commanded Bilal, who gave the adhan and iqamah. He prayed, then delivered a sermon and said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul﴾ until the end of the verse, ﴿indeed Allah is ever, over you, an Watcher﴾ [An-Nisa: 1]. And he recited the verse in al-Hashr: ﴿Let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾.

A man gave in charity from his dinar, from his dirham, from his garment, from a sa' of his wheat, from a sa' of his dates, until he said: 'Even with half a date.' Then a man from the Ansar came with a bag, his hand almost unable to carry it, rather it was unable to carry it. Then the people followed one another until I saw two heaps of food and clothing, until I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brightening as if it were gold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without anything being diminished from their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, he will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, without anything being diminished from their burdens.'"

Muslim alone narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, with a chain similar to this (Al-Musnad (4/358) and Sahih Muslim no. (1017)).

So His saying, ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah﴾, is a command to have taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of Allah) of Him, and it includes doing what one has been commanded and abstaining from what one has been forbidden.

* *

His saying, ﴿Let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾, means: take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, and consider what you have stored up for yourselves of righteous deeds for the Day of your return and your presentation before your Lord. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ is a second emphasis. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ means: know that He is Knowing of all your deeds and your conditions, nothing of you is hidden from Him, and nothing of your affairs, great or small, is absent from Him.

And He said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾, meaning: do not forget the remembrance of Allah, lest He cause you to forget working for the good of your own souls that will benefit you on your return. Indeed, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. For this reason He said: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who have departed from the obedience of Allah, who will perish on the Day of Resurrection, who will be losers on the day of their return, as He said: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 9].

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Hawti narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Hariz ibn Uthman narrated to us, from Nu'aym ibn Namhah, who said: In the sermon of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) was: "Do you not know that you go forth and return for a known term? Whoever is able to fulfil his term while in the service of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, let him do so, and you will not attain that except through Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, a people made their terms for others, so Allah has forbidden you to be like them: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾. Where are those among your brothers whom you know? They have gone forth with what they sent ahead in the days of their predecessors, and they have departed with wretchedness and happiness. Where are the first tyrants who built cities and fortified them with walls? They have become beneath the rock and the wells. This is the Book of Allah, whose wonders do not perish, so seek illumination from it for a day of darkness, [and be illuminated by its light and clarification]. Indeed Allah praised Zakariyya and his household, saying: ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, and they invoked Us in hope and fear, and they were humble before Us﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 90]. There is no good in speech not intended for the countenance of Allah, no good in wealth not spent in the cause of Allah, no good in one whose ignorance overcomes his forbearance, and no good in one who fears, regarding Allah, the blame of any blamer."

(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/60).)

This is a good chain (isnad), all of whose narrators are trustworthy (thiqat). The teacher of Hariz ibn Uthman, Nu'aym ibn Namhah, I do not know, neither by negation nor affirmation. However, Abu Dawud al-Sijistani ruled that all of Hariz's teachers are trustworthy. Witnesses (shawahid) to this sermon have been narrated through other channels. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal; the companions of Paradise – they are the attainers of success﴾, means (blank in manuscript) that these two groups are not equal in the judgment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is their judgment﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 21]. And He said: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer﴾ [Ghafir: 58].
