Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim (commentary on Surah 59, verses 21–24):

He, exalted is He, says, glorifying the matter of the Qur'an and showing its great rank, and that hearts ought to be humbled by it and split apart when they hear it, because of the promise and the binding warning it contains: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split asunder from fear of God.﴾ That is: if the mountain, in its hardness and firmness, were to understand this Qur'an and reflect on what is in it, it would be humbled and split apart from the fear of God, Mighty and Majestic. So how fitting is it for you, O mankind, that your hearts should not soften, humble themselves, and split apart from the fear of God, when you have understood from God His command and have reflected on His Book? Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And these parables We present to mankind, that perhaps they will reflect.﴾

Al-'Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain [you would have seen it humbled]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript M.]] to the end, he said: "If I had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain and loaded it with it, it would have split apart and been humbled from its weight and from the fear of God." So God commanded people, when the Qur'an is revealed to them, to receive it with intense fear and humility. Then He said: "Thus God presents parables to mankind, that perhaps they will reflect." Qatadah and Ibn Jarir said the same.

It is established in the mutawatir hadith [[Mutawatir: a report transmitted by so many narrators in every generation that its authenticity is beyond doubt.]] that when the pulpit was made for the Messenger of God ﷺ, he used to stand beside one of the trunks of the mosque on the day of the sermon. When the pulpit was first placed, and the Prophet ﷺ came to deliver the sermon, he passed the trunk toward the pulpit. At that, the trunk cried out and began to moan as a child moans when he is quieted, because of the remembrance and revelation it had heard near him. In some narrations of this hadith, al-Hasan al-Basri said after relating it: "You are more deserving than the trunk to long for the Messenger of God ﷺ." [[Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi related it, as cited in the author's al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (6/132), by way of Shayban ibn Farrukh, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from al-Hasan, from Anas, in the story of the trunk. He then added: "Al-Hasan, whenever he related this hadith, would weep and then say: 'O servants of God, the piece of wood longs for the Messenger of God out of longing for him because of his station with God. So you are more deserving to long for meeting him.'"]] And likewise this noble verse: if solid mountains, were they to hear the speech of God and understand it, would be humbled and split apart from fear of Him, then how about you, when you have heard and understood it? God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains were moved, or the earth was split open, or the dead were made to speak...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31], and it has already been mentioned that its meaning is: "Then this Qur'an would have been [that]." And He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, among them are those that split open and water emerges from them, and indeed, among them are those that fall down from fear of God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74].

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He is God, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.﴾ He informs that He is the One other than whom there is no god, so there is no lord besides Him, and no deity for existence other than Him, and everything worshipped besides Him is false. And that He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, that is, He knows all beings, those that are visible to us and those that are hidden from us, so nothing in the earth or in the heavens is concealed from Him, whether great or small, minor or major, even the smallest particle in darkness.

* *

As for His words: ﴿He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, the discussion of this has already been presented at the beginning of the tafsir [[Tafsir: the science of explaining and interpreting the Qur'an.]], which suffices without repeating it here. The meaning is that He possesses a vast mercy that encompasses all created beings. He is the Merciful of this world and the Hereafter, and their Especially Merciful. God, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 156], and He said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 54], and He said: ﴿Say: "By the bounty of God and by His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [Yunus: 58].

* *

As for His words, ﴿He is God, other than whom there is no deity, the King﴾, that is, the Possessor of all things, who disposes of them without any hindrance or opposition.

* *

As for His words, ﴿the Holy﴾: Wahb ibn Munabbih said: that is, the Pure. Mujahid and Qatadah said: that is, the Blessed. Ibn Jurayj said: the noble angels sanctify Him.

﴿the Peace﴾: that is, free from all defects and deficiencies, through His perfection in His essence, attributes, and actions.

* *

As for His words, ﴿the Granter of Security﴾: al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, He grants security to His creation from being wronged by Him. Qatadah said: He affirmed through His word that it is true. Ibn Zayd said: He confirmed His believing servants in their faith in Him.

* *

As for His words, ﴿the Guardian﴾: Ibn 'Abbas and others said: that is, the Witness over His creation regarding their deeds, meaning He is their watcher, as in His words: ﴿And God is Witness over all things﴾ [al-Buruj: 9], and His words: ﴿Then God is Witness over what they do﴾ [Yunus: 46].

* *

As for His words: ﴿Is then He who is standing over every soul in what it has earned [like others]?﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Ra'd: 33].

* *

As for His words, ﴿the Mighty﴾: that is, the One who has overcome all things, subdued them, and prevailed over them, so that His dominion cannot be reached, because of His might, greatness, majesty, and supremacy. Therefore He said: ﴿the Compeller, the Majestic﴾, that is, the One to whom alone compulsion is fitting, and to whom alone greatness is due because of His magnificence, as was mentioned in the authentic hadith: "Greatness is My waist-wrapper and majesty is My cloak, so whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will punish him."

Qatadah said: "al-Jabbar" is the One who compels His creation to what He wills. Ibn Jarir said: "al-Jabbar" is the One who sets right the affairs of His creation and disposes of them in what is good for them. Qatadah said: "al-Mutakabbir" means exalted above every evil.

Then He said: ﴿Glory be to God above what they associate with Him.﴾ [[In manuscript M: "yasifun" ("they describe"), which is an error.]]

* *

As for His words, ﴿He is God, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾: al-khalq means measuring out (al-taqdir), and al-bara' means al-fary, which is execution and bringing into existence what He has measured and decreed. Not everyone who measures out something and arranges it is able to carry it out and bring it into being, except God, Mighty and Majestic. A poet praising another said:

"Indeed you carry out what you have created [measured out], while some people create but do not carry through."

That is: you execute what you have created, that is, what you have measured out, unlike others, who are unable to accomplish what they intend. So khalq is taqdir (measuring out), and fary is tanfidh (execution). From this one says: "The executioner measured out, then cut," meaning he cut in accordance with what he measured out and what he intended.

* *

As for His words, ﴿the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾: that is, He who, when He wills something, says to it "Be," and it is, in the attribute He wills and the form He chooses. Like His words: ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾ [al-Infitar: 8]. Therefore He said: ﴿the Fashioner﴾, that is, the One who executes what He wills to bring into existence in the attribute He desires.

* *

As for His words: ﴿To Him belong the best names﴾: the discussion of this has already been presented in Surah al-A'raf, along with the hadith transmitted in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Indeed, God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise, and He is Witr (One), and He loves what is odd." Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also narrated it, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with an additional passage after his words "and He is Witr, He loves what is odd." The wording here is that of al-Tirmidhi: "He is God, other than whom there is no god: the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Forgiving, the Subduer, the Bestower, the Provider, the Opener, the All-Knowing, the Restrainer, the Expander, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Giver of honor, the Giver of humiliation, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Forbearing, the Magnificent, the Forgiving, the Appreciative, the Most High, the Great, the Preserver, the Sustainer, the Reckoner, the Majestic, the Generous, the Watchful, the Responsive, the Vast, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Resurrector, the Witness, the Truth, the Trustee, the Strong, the Firm, the Protector, the Praiseworthy, the Enumerator, the Originator, the Restorer, the Giver of life, the Giver of death, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Perceiver, the Noble, the One, the Eternal Refuge, the Capable, the Omnipotent, the One who brings forward, the One who delays, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Patron, the Exalted, the Benevolent, the Oft-Relenting, the Avenger, the Pardoner, the Kind, Master of the Kingdom, Possessor of Majesty and Honor, the Equitable, the Gatherer, the Self-Sufficient, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Harmer, the Benefactor, the Light, the Guide, the Originator, the Enduring, the Heir, the Rightly-Guided, the Patient."

The version in Ibn Majah differs with additions, omissions, and changes of order. We have already presented this hadith at length, with its chains and wordings, which suffices without repeating it here. [[Its takhrij (tracing of sources) was mentioned in the commentary on verse 180 of Surah al-A'raf.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him﴾, like His words: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [God] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [al-Isra': 44].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, that is, His presence cannot be approached, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His legislation and His decree.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, Khalid, that is Ibn Tahman Abu al-'Ala' al-Khaffaf, related to us, from Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever says three times in the morning, 'I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan,' and then recites the last three verses of Surah al-Hashr, God will assign to him seventy thousand angels who will invoke blessings upon him until evening. If he dies that day, he dies a martyr. And whoever says them in the evening has the same rank."

Therefore He said: ﴿the Fashioner﴾, that is, the One who executes what He wills to bring into existence in the attribute He desires.

* *

As for His words: ﴿To Him belong the best names﴾: the discussion of this has already been presented in Surah al-A'raf, along with the hadith transmitted in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Indeed, God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise, and He is Witr (One), and He loves what is odd." Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also narrated it, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with an additional passage after his words "and He is Witr, He loves what is odd." The wording here is that of al-Tirmidhi: "He is God, other than whom there is no god: the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Forgiving, the Subduer, the Bestower, the Provider, the Opener, the All-Knowing, the Restrainer, the Expander, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Giver of honor, the Giver of humiliation, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Forbearing, the Magnificent, the Forgiving, the Appreciative, the Most High, the Great, the Preserver, the Sustainer, the Reckoner, the Majestic, the Generous, the Watchful, the Responsive, the Vast, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Resurrector, the Witness, the Truth, the Trustee, the Strong, the Firm, the Protector, the Praiseworthy, the Enumerator, the Originator, the Restorer, the Giver of life, the Giver of death, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Perceiver, the Noble, the One, the Eternal Refuge, the Capable, the Omnipotent, the One who brings forward, the One who delays, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Patron, the Exalted, the Benevolent, the Oft-Relenting, the Avenger, the Pardoner, the Kind, Master of the Kingdom, Possessor of Majesty and Honor, the Equitable, the Gatherer, the Self-Sufficient, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Harmer, the Benefactor, the Light, the Guide, the Originator, the Enduring, the Heir, the Rightly-Guided, the Patient."

The version in Ibn Majah differs with additions, omissions, and changes of order. We have already presented this hadith at length, with its chains and wordings, which suffices without repeating it here. [[Its takhrij (tracing of sources) was mentioned in the commentary on verse 180 of Surah al-A'raf.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him﴾, like His words: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [God] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [al-Isra': 44].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, that is, His presence cannot be approached, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His legislation and His decree.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, Khalid, that is Ibn Tahman Abu al-'Ala' al-Khaffaf, related to us, from Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever says three times in the morning, 'I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan,' and then recites the last three verses of Surah al-Hashr, God will assign to him seventy thousand angels who will invoke blessings upon him until evening. If he dies that day, he dies a martyr. And whoever says them in the evening has the same rank."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, with the same chain [[Al-Musnad (5/26) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2922.]], and he said: "It is gharib (a hadith with a single narration at some point in its chain); we do not know it except through this route."
